gh api repos/CircleCI-Labs/machine-runner-swarm/commits/main/status --jq '.statuses[].context'
data.cost-and-duration#Cost and duration:
Measured on 2026-10-13 (pipeline 9aed4106, a full run on smr-swarm/ci). Credits use the published per-minute rates (Windows medium 40, Linux xlarge 40, Linux medium and Arm medium 10, Docker small 5, Docker medium 10). The e2e probes run on self-hosted classes and cost no compute credits.
Pipeline Credits (about) Wall clock Feature branch that changes a file every suite reads (measured with both Windows jobs) 1,500, of which the two Windows jobs are 1,200 18 min main (every job except release) 3,800 25 min A documentation-only pull request 200 The weekly security scan 150 a run The measurements predate the gating: a feature branch now costs about 700 credits less (no Server 2025 job) and about 500 less when no Windows file changes (an estimate). Windows dominates the cost: every Windows job pulls the 2 GB Server Core image onto a fresh VM (about 5 to 10 minutes, in a step with no_output_timeout: 30m), and windows-swarm-ltsc2022 takes 12 min 31 s and windows-swarm-ltsc2025 about 17 min. Splitting linux-swarm bills about 1,200 credits instead of about 1,100, because three more VMs pull and set up, and the wall clock falls from about 27 minutes to about 9.
data.create-the-schedule#Create the schedule:
The workflow runs when the pipeline parameter security-scan is true. Nothing in the repository creates the schedule: a maintainer does this once. Use the branch main, so the scan reads the pins of main. The schedule runs every Monday at 06:00 UTC, after Renovate has opened its pull requests.
In the web app, open Project Settings, Project Setup (or Triggers), select Schedule + next to the pipeline, and set: name weekly-security-scan, branch main, pipeline attribution “The scheduling system”, parameter security-scan = true, repeats weekly on Monday, start time 06 (UTC), 1 time per hour. Enable the trigger and save.
The CircleCI CLI has no command for schedules. With the API, create a personal API token, keep it in CIRCLECI_TOKEN (never in a repository file, never printed), and run:
curl --request POST "https://circleci.com/api/v2/project/gh/CircleCI-Labs/machine-runner-swarm/schedule" \ --header "circle-token: ${CIRCLECI_TOKEN}" \ --header "Content-Type: application/json" \ --data '{ "name": "weekly-security-scan", "description": "Trivy on every pinned image and govulncheck on the proxy (docs/ci.md, Security scan)", "attribution-actor": "system", "parameters": {"branch": "main", "security-scan": true}, "timetable": {"per-hour": 1, "hours-of-day": [6], "days-of-week": ["MON"]} }'
data.deploys#Deploys:
The pipeline records its deployments in the Deploys view of CircleCI, with deploy markers: circleci run release plan creates the deploy as pending, and circleci run release update moves it to RUNNING and then to SUCCESS or FAILED. CircleCI creates the components and environments on the first deploy. ci/deploy-marker.sh makes the calls, and ci/tests/deploy-marker.sh tests it in lint-circleci against a stub of the circleci command.
Deploy Job Component Environment Version A GitHub release release machine-runner-swarm github-releases The release tag, for example v0.2.0 The docs site docs-site-publish docs-site github-pages The commit SHA The token proxy image of a commit proxy-image-publish token-proxy-image docker-hub sha-<12 characters of the commit> The release tags of the image release token-proxy-image docker-hub The release number, X.Y.Z Only a real deploy is recorded. The release job plans its deploy after it has the version, and only when it will publish (GITHUB_TOKEN is set). Nothing to release and a run without the token record nothing. The docs job records a deploy only with GITHUB_TOKEN, and the image jobs only with the Docker Hub credentials. Failure. The release script gives the deploy FAILED, with the exit status as the reason, on every way out of the script. A failed or canceled deploy gives the live version back to the last successful one. The docs job does the same in a step with when: on_fail. Cancel. A cancel that reaches ci/release.sh as a signal records CANCELED. The long step of docs-site-publish and proxy-image-publish runs under ci/deploy-marker.sh guard NAME COMMAND, which stops the command on SIGTERM or SIGINT, gives the deploy CANCELED and exits 143. A canceled step runs no later step (not even when: on_fail), so without the guard the deploy would stay RUNNING. Only a real cancel shows whether CircleCI sends the signal to the step. The plan comes after the build. docs-site-publish builds first and plans afterwards, so a site that does not build is a failed job, not a FAILED deploy. One job. Plan and updates are steps of one job. A rerun from failed that starts a new job would break the link between them, and CircleCI refuses a second final status for a deploy. A marker never fails a job. If the task agent refuses a call (for example the organization has no Deploys), the script prints a warning and exits 0.
data.docs-site#Docs site:
The documentation is also a site on GitHub Pages: https://circleci-labs.github.io/machine-runner-swarm/. CircleCI builds it with Hugo and the Hextra theme and pushes it to the gh-pages branch. No GitHub Actions workflow is involved. The Markdown of README.md, docs/, CHANGELOG.md and CONTRIBUTING.md stays the only source, and nothing in it is written for the site: README.md is the home page.
Add every new, renamed or removed page to site/nav.txt. site/stage.sh fails on a docs/*.md file that the list misses and on a listed file that does not exist, so docs-site-build catches a page that would be missing from the sidebar. STAGE_LENIENT=1 turns both errors into warnings while you restructure. Hextra renders GitHub alerts, tables, fenced code in lists, {{ }} and text in code, and Mermaid blocks as GitHub does. A Mermaid block renders in the browser: without JavaScript the reader sees the source.
data.docs-site-previews#Docs site previews:
Every branch and pull request gets a preview from docs-site-build. The production build links to its pages under /machine-runner-swarm/, so it works only at the GitHub Pages address, while CircleCI serves a job’s artifacts from https://output.circle-artifacts.com/output/job//artifacts// with a new job id on every run. site/preview.sh therefore builds a second copy, site/public-preview, with relative URLs and uglyURLs (a page is a file, ci.html). It makes every relative link name a file (an artifacts server does not serve the index.html of a directory) and removes integrity attributes (CircleCI serves script files from another origin, and a browser refuses a script with an integrity hash from there), and lychee checks the result.
The job stores the preview as the artifacts docs-site-preview, and prints and stores the address:
Docs preview: https://output.circle-artifacts.com/output/job//artifacts/0/docs-site-preview/index.html A comment on the pull request (optional). docs-site-build has no context, so no token is in the environment of Hugo, lychee, the Go modules or the site/ scripts. docs-site-comment holds scalable-machine-runner-pr-comments, requires docs-site-build, and runs only for a push that has a pull request (the gate passes pull-request: true when CIRCLE_PULL_REQUEST is a GitHub pull request address). With a GITHUB_PR_COMMENT_TOKEN, site/preview-comment.sh posts ONE comment with the address and updates it on later pushes. Without the token, without a pull request, or when GitHub refuses a call, it skips the comment and the job stays green. It sends the token to curl on standard input, so the token is in no command line and no log. To turn the comment on, a maintainer does this once:
Create a fine-grained personal access token for a dedicated bot account that is on no bypass list and has no other access: resource owner CircleCI-Labs, only this repository, repository permission Issues: Read and write, nothing else. A pull request comment is an issue comment, and the script calls only the issue comment endpoints. Do not use a maintainer’s token: Pull requests: Read and write would also let it submit approving reviews and edit or close pull requests, as its owner.
Create the context scalable-machine-runner-pr-comments with the variable GITHUB_PR_COMMENT_TOKEN. The job already names the context. Without the variable it posts nothing.
Restrict the context to this project and refuse SSH reruns:
circleci context restriction create scalable-machine-runner-pr-comments --org --type project --value circleci context restriction create scalable-machine-runner-pr-comments --org --type expression \ --value 'not job.ssh.enabled and not (pipeline.config_source starts-with "api")'
data.documentation-only-changes#Documentation:
A push that changes only documentation runs lint and the docs site build. A path is documentation when it is under docs/ or site/, or is a Markdown file. The exception is docs/microvm.md: linux/tests/microvm.sh reads its Docker configuration from it.
Not known. A missing base, a failed git fetch and an empty list all mean “not known”, and everything runs. So does full: true. Releases. On main, when a commit of the push would release, the push is not documentation only and the whole pipeline runs. Publishing continues. The workflow docs-site is not affected: a docs change on main is published and recorded as a deploy. Required checks. GitHub shows one status for each workflow. Require the workflow ci and nothing else (A ruleset for main).
data.e2e-a-runner-hosted-inside-a-circleci-jo: Both e2e groups follow one pattern. Job A (the host, a cloud VM with the e2e context) installs the stack and hosts the runner as a Swarm service for the resource class cci-labs/scalable-machine-runner-e2e-. The probe jobs (B) are ordinary jobs on that class, without the context. B1 leaves residue, and B2 is scheduled after B1 and must find a different container and none of the residue. A verifies independently of the probes, from docker events, and prints the verdict.
data.facts-about-the-ci-machines-that-the-des:
Measured on 2026-10-12. Check these first when something Swarm-related breaks in CI.
Fact Consequence Linux machine image ubuntu-2604:2026.05.1: Docker 29.4.2 with the containerd image store (overlayfs snapshotter), on x86_64 and arm64 The writable layer is upperdir=/var/lib/containerd/io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.overlayfs/snapshots/N/fs, and the probes hash it A service with hostname: "{{.Node.Hostname}}--{{.Task.Slot}}" (the shipped Linux stack) gives every container of a slot the same hostname Probes read the full container ID from /proc/self/mountinfo (Docker bind-mounts /etc/hostname from /var/lib/docker/containers//) and compare the writable-layer hash. The host maps the container ID to the Nth start event of the service docker events prints an empty exitCode for start events The event format uses {{or (index .Actor.Attributes "exitCode") "-"}}, or the columns shift Windows machine images (Server 2022 build 20348, Server 2025 build 26100): Docker 29.4.0, default isolation process Containers share the host kernel. data.github-pages-and-the-token#GitHub Pages:
A maintainer does this once:
Create the context scalable-machine-runner-docs with the variable GITHUB_TOKEN: a fine-grained token for this repository only, repository permission Contents: read and write, nothing else. Without the variable the job builds and checks the site and publishes nothing.
Restrict the context to this project and to main:
circleci context restriction create scalable-machine-runner-docs --org --type project --value circleci context restriction create scalable-machine-runner-docs --org --type expression \ --value 'pipeline.git.branch == "main" and not job.ssh.enabled and not (pipeline.config_source starts-with "api")' After the first publication, open Settings, Pages, and set Source to Deploy from a branch, the branch to gh-pages and the folder to / (root). data.linux#Linux:
e2e-linux (job group, serial-group /e2e-linux) e2e-linux-host (A) ci/e2e-host.sh prepare | run | cleanup | sweep e2e-linux-b1 (B1) service linux-default e2e-linux-b2 (B2) service linux-default, requires B1; holds 75 s while the host restarts the token proxy e2e-linux-b3 (B3) service linux-hardened, requires B2 e2e-linux-arm64 (job group, the same serial-group, requires e2e-linux) e2e-linux-arm64-host and -b1, -b2, -b3: the same on arm.medium The host:
prepare is sudo linux/setup.sh --swarm-init (a manager, where the token proxy runs with no label), the documented path: the shipped runner-distributor installs the runner. It also builds the token proxy image of the checkout (docker build proxy/) on the VM, the only node, because the job has no registry. run creates the secrets linux-default-token and linux-hardened-token from E2E_RUNNER_TOKEN_LINUX through setup.sh --secret, plus the placeholder runner-placeholder-token that the runners read. Each secret is a runner config file (api.auth_token), target circleci_runner_config.yaml, uid 2000, mode 0400. The token travels on stdin, never in a file or on a command line, and only the token proxy mounts the class secrets. It deploys the shipped linux/stack/runners.yaml with MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_PROXY_IMAGE set to the image it built, and a generated override that gives the active service one replica of a digest-pinned stock cimg/base, a 5 minute idle timeout and a bind mount for the evidence directory. Every other runner service gets zero replicas. The runner service waits up to 10 minutes for the runner-distributor. Phase 1 is linux-default for B1 and B2. While B2 holds its job, the host restarts the token proxy, and B2 must pass: the real runner and task agent survive a proxy restart against the real API, and the restart restores the runner that claimed (the start line says state restored and 1 runner(s) have claimed). When B2 reports, the host removes the stack at once so a replacement container cannot claim the next probe. Phase 2 is linux-hardened (MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_JOB_SUDO=false) for B3. Both services use the same class token, so only one is deployed at a time. The probes (ci/e2e-probe.sh):
The first step checks that /e2e-evidence/host names this workflow: a probe claimed by a stray runner fails there. Residue: B1 plants files in $HOME, /tmp, /var/tmp and (with sudo) /etc. Every probe fails if it finds an earlier probe’s files. Identity: the container ID (from /proc/self/mountinfo) and the writable-layer hash must differ from the previous probe’s. The job runs as circleci, the runner as circleci-runner, the entrypoint logged stepdown=sudo (default) or stepdown=setpriv no_new_privs=yes (hardened), and sudo -n true works in the default service only. Token readability, recorded in the evidence. As the job user, without and with sudo, the probe tries to read /run/secrets/circleci_runner_config.yaml (byte counts only), counts other users’ readable /proc/PID/environ, and checks the job environment, every command line and, through sudo, the runner’s environment for the token’s variable and key names (names only). The token must be in none of them, and a read without sudo must fail in both services. In the hardened service sudo must be unusable. In the default service the sudo outcome is recorded and not asserted, because root can read the token. The last step writes passed or failed to /e2e-evidence/..status, so the host stops at once on a failed probe.
data.linux-jobs-without-a-token#Linux jobs wi:
The four linux-swarm jobs need no secret. They are one job definition with a groups parameter that holds the arguments of linux/tests/run-all.sh. Each starts its own single-node and two-node Swarm inside privileged docker:dind containers (the CI VM’s engine never becomes a Swarm node), downloads from a local HTTP mirror, fails when one of its groups fails, and prints a RESULT line per group.
Job Groups Time (estimate, with about 2 minutes of pulls and setup) linux-swarm-distributor distributor 8.5 min linux-swarm-proxy proxy (the token proxy image in a Swarm) 8.5 min linux-swarm-a stack-config, helper, ephemerality, exit80, token, task 6.3 min linux-swarm-b placement, persistent, drain, limits, network, container-mode, bats 7.3 min To move a group, change the lists in continue.yml: lint-circleci compares them with linux/tests/run-all.sh --list and fails when a group is in no list or in two. Each job is skipped on a documentation-only change and is a requirement of the release.
linux-setup and linux-arm64 run ci/linux-smoke.sh on a fresh VM: linux/setup.sh --check, then --swarm-init twice (the second run must be a no-op), then setup.sh --deploy with a made-up token (the runner gets 401 from CircleCI, which does not matter here). The runner-distributor service downloads the pinned release from CircleCI’s real manifest, and the job waits for its link current. The job then checks that:
the volume runner-bin is root-owned and not writable by others, its SHA256 record equals the hash of the binary, and /opt/machine-runner-swarm does not exist on the host; the runner reports its version unmodified in a stock cimg/base with -v runners_runner-bin:/opt/machine-runner-swarm:ro, and circleci-runner-entrypoint with a config file but no runner name exits 80; in the running linux-default and linux-hardened containers the runner runs as circleci-runner, the container mounts only the placeholder config, and the job user cannot read /run/secrets/circleci_runner_config.yaml or another user’s process environment; linux-default keeps sudo, and sudo can read the placeholder config (the class token is in the token proxy, which this test stops), and linux-hardened has no sudo. linux-image-example builds the bring-your-own-image example and scans it. Trivy policy:
The SBOM (CycloneDX) and the HIGH/CRITICAL reports are artifacts: reports/sbom-example.cdx.json, reports/trivy-example.{json,txt}. The gate fails on a fixable CRITICAL finding that the image adds on top of cimg/base (the scan of the base is subtracted). The base is upstream, and its findings stay visible in the reports. The runner is not in the image. Exceptions go in .trivyignore, one CVE per line, with a reason, an owner and an exp: date, after which Trivy stops honouring the entry. Use one only for findings this repository cannot fix.
data.linux-microvm#linux-microvm: linux-microvm runs linux/tests/microvm.sh on the Android machine image, the only CircleCI machine image with nested virtualization (/dev/kvm, /dev/vhost-vsock, and a Docker that runs privileged containers). The job loads vhost_vsock and vhost_net, installs zstd, and sets SWARM_TEST_REQUIRE_KVM=1, so a missing /dev/kvm fails the job instead of skipping. The script downloads the pinned Kata release (about 1 GB, SHA-256 checked), starts a runc manager and a Kata worker in Docker-in-Docker containers, and deploys the real runners.yaml and microvm.yaml with the real entrypoint, the real runner against a fake API, and a fake runner. See MicroVM jobs for the checks. The job passed in each of its first three pipelines, so it is a requirement of the release. Run the script locally on any host with KVM: it skips without /dev/kvm.

data.not-tested#Not tested: Gap What it means A real multi-host cluster, a mixed Linux and Windows cluster, overlay traffic between nodes The Linux suite runs two Swarm nodes as containers on one VM, and every Windows test runs on one host. Only isolation between classes on one Swarm is tested docker node update --availability drain with a busy replica, a rolling update with a real runner mid-job, update order with several busy replicas, scale-down while jobs run, --update-parallelism The stop paths are tested with a fake job, and a real runner only while idle Token rotation, the leaked-token procedure, manager loss, quorum, backup, restore, autolock, certificate rotation Documented in Operations, not run in CI The persistent class with a real task agent, and the docker-build add-on with a real job Linux and Windows run a fake or an idle runner. The Windows named pipe is never used by a test Real jobs in a microVM, Kata on arm64 or AMD CPUs, clouds other than AWS microvm.sh runs the real runner against a fake API on nested KVM on AWS (Intel). Checkout, caches and artifacts over virtiofs are not exercised RHEL and SELinux, Windows Server 2019, Hyper-V isolation, group managed service accounts, proxies, add_ssh_keys Not exercised, and the docs say so Rerun job with SSH (ssh-rerun.yaml) CI checks that the files parse, merge and keep the contract, including host-mode port 54782, max_replicas_per_node: 1 and the advertise address. The Swarm side was proven by hand on a Linux Swarm with a real runner: the Enable SSH step runs, and the task agent answers on port 54782 of the node. Each has its own tests, and nothing runs both on the same input. Two known differences: Linux flips current with one atomic rename, while Windows removes and recreates the link, so a container that starts in between does not start and Swarm retries (Upgrade the runner on Windows); file:// is accepted on Windows only publish() of the release job It stops before publishing without GITHUB_TOKEN, so the first release is its first real run. data.pinned-versions#Pinned versions:
Every tool image is pinned by tag and digest, and every download by version and SHA-256. Renovate, the GitHub App of the organization, keeps them current. renovate.json is its whole configuration: the repository needs no workflow or token for it.
When. Renovate opens pull requests on Monday before 06:00 UTC, at most six at a time. A major version waits for approval on the Dependency Dashboard. Commit types. A pull request that changes what users run (stack images, proxy image bases, Go toolchain for the proxy image, Windows distributor tools) is a fix(deps) commit, so the release job makes a release for it. proxy image bases are the distroless base of proxy/Dockerfile and the Nano Server digests of ci/Build-ProxyImage.ps1: as ci(deps), which cliff.toml skips, the published image would keep stale base layers until an unrelated feat or fix lands. The CI-only groups are ci(deps) and the theme is docs(deps): they make no release (Releasing). Digests. Renovate pins every image that carries a digest, refreshes the digest of a tag, and moves the tag and digest together. cimg/base and the e2e sweeper image circleci/runner-agent get a new digest but never a new tag: a person changes the tag. Pin Where How Renovate finds it Images with a digest .circleci/*.yml, linux/stack/*.yaml, windows/stack/*.yaml, ci/, the tests, the docs One regex manager for name:tag@sha256:... in any file Hugo, lychee, the CircleCI CLI docs-site command and lint-circleci in continue.yml A # renovate: comment above the version variable git-cliff, cosign, crane, gh, Go, govulncheck ci/release.sh, ci/tools.sh (cosign, crane), ci/security-scan.sh The same comment Kata Containers KATA_VERSION in linux/tests/microvm.sh A regex (GitHub releases) PortableGit, 7-Zip ReleaseTag and SevenZipVersion in windows/stack/runner-distributor.ps1 A regex each (GitHub releases) To pin a new tool, put its version in one variable and add the comment # renovate: datasource=github-releases depName=/ extractVersion=^v(?.*)$ on the line above it. The comment is the whole configuration. The versions in use are in the files of the table: continue.yml names every CI image and tool.
data.pins-that-stay-by-hand#Pins that stay by:
Renovate does not touch these. Change the version and its checksum together, and run the check of the job that uses it.
Images without a digest in the stack files (coredns/coredns, alpine:3.24 of the token proxy, the cimg classes) and the Windows servercore tags: the tag is a choice for users, and Windows tags must match the host. The weekly security scan still scans them (not the Windows images). The Linux and Windows machine images (executors in continue.yml): ubuntu-2604:2026.05.1, windows-server-2022-gui:2026.05.1, windows-server-2025-gui:2026.05.1. They use dated tags, not current, which CircleCI moves every three months: an image that changes under an unrelated pull request would turn it red. Every quarter, read the image changelog, move those three tags together, and start a pipeline for the branch with full: true. The Android machine image for linux-microvm: android:current. CircleCI publishes quarterly tags plus current (gen2) and default (gen1), not dated tags. Bump it by hand when the image changelog says to. PSScriptAnalyzer and Pester (lint-powershell, windows-swarm, windows/tests/Invoke-UnitTests.ps1). The Mermaid script of the site (params.mermaid.base in site/hugo.yaml): it must match the version that the lint-docs-mermaid image bundles. The runner build of the e2e sweeper: the image tag in ci/e2e-host.sh and the circleci-runner.exe URL and SHA-256 in ci/E2E-Host.ps1 move together. Install Hugo extended 0.168.0 and Go (Hugo downloads the theme as a Go module), then run from the repository root:
site/stage.sh cd site && hugo server Run site/stage.sh again after you change a page. To run the pipeline check, add lychee and run (cd site && hugo --minify --panicOnWarning) && site/check.sh.
data.publishing-fails-closed-on-main#Publishi:
A missing publishing credential must not leave main green with nothing published. The gate sets strict to true on main when both e2e tokens are present (the production project). A documentation-only change and the path gate do not turn it off. The jobs that publish get REQUIRE_CREDENTIALS=true: proxy-image-linux and proxy-image-windows (publish variants, in a first step), proxy-image-publish, proxy-image-edge, release and docs-site-publish. If DOCKERHUB_USERNAME, DOCKERHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN is missing, the job fails and names the context.
Elsewhere the publication is skipped with a message and the pipeline stays green: a project without the contexts, a fork, any branch. ci/tests/require-credentials.sh tests both behaviors.
publish is on for main when proxy-image is on and the push is not documentation only. A main push that does not touch the proxy image publishes nothing.
data.release#Release:
The release job is part of the ci workflow. On main with both e2e tokens and a commit that would make a release, the setup phase passes release: true together with every suite, full-suite, e2e-linux and e2e-windows, so every job that the release requires really runs. It requires every other job of the workflow except the three that lint-circleci names in its $optional list (linux-mixed-arch, proxy-image-edge, docs-site-comment). Other branches never run it, and neither do tag pipelines (the release creates the tag, and CircleCI schedules no job for a tag).
Job Executor What it does release cimg/base:2026.10, contexts scalable-machine-runner-release and scalable-machine-runner-dockerhub, serial-group ci/release.sh: the Swarm config name check, version, notes, the digest of the token proxy image pinned in the stack files, bundles, SHA256SUMS, keyless signature, the signature check and release tags of the image, and the GitHub release. Without GITHUB_TOKEN or the Docker Hub credentials it stops before publishing Add every new job to requires of the release job. lint-circleci fails when a job is missing: it compiles the workflow and checks that every job that no other job requires is a requirement of the release (in the compiled workflow the release waits for one lock job that requires them). See Releasing for the rules, the token setup, and recovery from a failed release.
data.release-jobs-stay-consistent#Release job: The release job requires every other job, so its parameter is on only when every suite is: main, both tokens, and a commit that would release. A push to main that would not release has release and proxy-image-edge off, and every job a gate turns off is required by no job that runs. lint-circleci checks that the release requires every job and that every job outside lint and docs-site-build has a suite filter. ci/tests/setup-gate.sh checks the same rules on every row.
data.running-the-checks-locally#Running the c:

data.secrets-and-public-logs#Secrets and publ:
The project is public, so job logs and artifacts are public.
The e2e context. The runner tokens live only in scalable-machine-runner-e2e. Its restrictions are this project and an expression that allows only the branches that may use it, with SSH reruns and API-started pipelines excluded. A restriction is a CircleCI organization setting that the config file cannot change, so a maintainer sets it ( and as in The Docker Hub context):
circleci context restriction create scalable-machine-runner-e2e --org --type project --value circleci context restriction create scalable-machine-runner-e2e --org --type expression \ --value '(pipeline.git.branch == "main" or pipeline.git.branch starts-with "smr-swarm/") and not job.ssh.enabled and not (pipeline.config_source starts-with "api")' The expression is the second line of defence: the when of the setup workflows already keeps the context off every other branch, and the restriction keeps an API pipeline (which can name any branch and, where the organization allows it, bring its own config) from using it. In the organization’s advanced settings, leave pipelines with an unversioned config off.
Project settings. The project is connected through the GitHub OAuth integration, not the GitHub App, and its slug is gh/CircleCI-Labs/machine-runner-swarm. In Project Settings, Advanced:
Build forked pull requests and Pass secrets to builds from forked pull requests must be off: a fork pull request would otherwise run its own .circleci/config.yml on this project. Auto-cancel redundant workflows must be off. With it on, every push to smr-swarm/* or a non-default branch cancels the running e2e workflow, and the host of a cancelled workflow can leave a Swarm service that claims the next pipeline’s job. With it off, each group’s serial-group runs one at a time and the newer one waits. Turn on the setting that requires an administrator to change project settings, and turn off SSH reruns if the organization offers them. Token handling. On Linux the token goes to docker secret create on stdin and is never on disk. On Windows it is in a file for the instant docker secret create reads it, outside the artifact directory. It is never printed, and the probes never print their environment.
data.security-scan#Security scan:
A weekly workflow, security-scan, looks for known vulnerabilities in what the repository pins. It is a workflow of its own in continue.yml, started by a schedule, and never runs the ci workflow: no build, no e2e job, no release. It has no context, so it holds no secret.
Job Executor What it checks security-scan-images ubuntu-2604:2026.05.1, Docker ci/security-scan.sh images: Trivy on every pinned image. The script finds them in the files: every reference with a digest (name:tag@sha256:...) and the image: of every stack file, so the cimg classes, CoreDNS and alpine:3.24 are in too. Trivy pulls each image from its registry (--image-src remote) and builds nothing security-scan-go golang:1.27.2, small ci/security-scan.sh go: govulncheck on proxy/ with the Go toolchain of the proxy builds. Fails on any vulnerability that the proxy calls, with a fix or not (a standard library fix means a new Go release) ci/security-scan-images.txt says how each image is treated, by repository name:
List What Effect infra What a stack runs as infrastructure on a user’s cluster: alpine (the distributor), ccilabs/machine-runner-swarm-proxy (the token proxy, tag edge; until the first publication the scan reports that it cannot pull it), coredns/coredns, registry.k8s.io/pause A CRITICAL finding with a fix fails the job, and so does an infra image that Trivy cannot scan report Job images that users choose (cimg/*) and images that only CI or a test uses HIGH and CRITICAL findings are listed and never fail the run: most carry some in any given week, from upstream packages that this repository cannot patch skip The Windows images Listed, not scanned: Trivy finds no operating system in a Windows image when it runs on Linux and returns an empty, clean report, so the scan would claim a result it does not have To add an image, add a line to ci/security-scan-images.txt. An image on no list fails the scan, and lint-circleci runs ci/security-scan.sh lists and fails the pull request that adds it.
What to do about a failure. The log ends with the answer: bump the digest (a Renovate pull request does it, Pinned versions), or add a justified .trivyignore entry (the CVE, the reason, an owner and an expiry date: the policy is in that file). An entry also applies to the trivy command of linux-image-example, which reads the same file but is a different check: it gates the image this repository builds, against its base.
data.stray-claims-timeouts-and-cleanup#Stray: Dedicated classes. Nothing else targets the two e2e classes. Serial groups. Host and probes form one job group with a serial-group per project, so two pipelines never run e2e runners at the same time. Both Windows groups share one key, because they share a resource class and token. Evidence and identity. A probe not claimed by this workflow’s host fails at its first step. A host whose container exits without the expected probe’s evidence fails at once. Timeouts. Each runner has idle_timeout 5m and max_run_time 10m on Linux and 15m on Windows. The host fails after 40 minutes, and steps have no_output_timeout. A 401 from the runner API fails the host within seconds: rotate the token. Cleanup always runs: the stack and secrets are removed and the VM leaves the swarm. A cancel removes the stack. Cancelling an e2e workflow releases the serial-group lock at once, and the idle service of the cancelled host would claim the B1 of the next pipeline. So ci/e2e-host.sh run traps SIGTERM and SIGINT and runs docker stack rm (ci/tests/e2e-sim.sh has the scenario terminated). ci/E2E-Host.ps1 -Mode Run does the same when PowerShell exits without having ended the run itself. Windows has no SIGTERM, and a kill that PowerShell cannot see leaves nothing to run: there the rule is a rerun. Keep Auto-cancel redundant workflows off. Sweep after a failure. If the host fails while a probe may still be queued, it runs a throwaway runner (the pinned circleci/runner-agent image on Linux, the SHA-256-verified circleci-runner.exe on Windows) for up to 2 minutes, so the probe is claimed and fails fast instead of holding the lock. If that cannot help (the token was rejected), cancel the workflow in the UI: the context holds no API token, so CI cannot cancel workflows itself.
data.tested#Tested: Area What is checked How Stack files Every file parses, merges and interpolates, and each service keeps its contract (secrets, mounts, placement, limits, capabilities). Every Swarm config is named after the content of its file lint-stack, ci/config-names.sh, stack-config.sh, Stack.Tests.ps1 Install on Linux setup.sh checks the node and starts Swarm twice, and the second run changes nothing. The shipped stack is deployed, its runner-distributor installs the pinned runner from the real manifest, and the runner runs in a stock cimg/base linux-setup, linux-arm64 Clean environment A new container for every job and no residue from the job before. A negative control shows that a plain restart reuses the container ephemerality.sh, Test-Ephemerality.ps1, the e2e on Linux and Windows 2022 and 2025 Step-down and the token The default class keeps sudo and can read the runner’s config file. The hardened class has no sudo, and a setuid binary cannot lift the job (setpriv --no-new-privs). The token is in no environment or command line token.sh, task.sh (the real runner binary against a fake API), the e2e probes Token proxy Each class claims with its own token, and no class token is in a runner container. One claim per container, 403 for a second claim and for a container that is not a runner, and a restarted proxy refuses only the runners that claimed. A proxy with no state for a class asks GET /api/v3/runner/scale with that class’s token: no running task lets the runners present claim, and running tasks or no usable answer refuse them all proxy-test, proxy.sh (phases order, lost, unknown, fresh) Token proxy image The Linux image (linux/amd64, arm64, ppc64le, s390x via QEMU) and the Windows image (ltsc2022, ltsc2025) build and run non-root, read-only and healthy. The publication runs against a registry of its own. The keyless signing and the ref check are rehearsed on a throwaway image in every pipeline. Pushing to Docker Hub is not tested in a pull request proxy-image-linux, proxy-image-windows-*, ci/tests/proxy-image.sh, signing-rehearsal Runner distributor Runners wait and exit 80, then start in the same container once it is released. A fresh and a joining node get the runner by themselves. An upgrade under three busy jobs leaves the jobs on their version, and a rollback needs no download. An exact pin never changes by itself, 3.1, 3 and current follow the manifest (never another line or major), and pruning keeps 3 versions. A tampered binary makes new containers exit 80 and is repaired, and a wrong SHA-256 installs nothing. Windows: the same against a local mirror, plus the real manifest distributor.sh, Test-Install.ps1, Test-Distributor.ps1 Runtime behavior Placement, stop and drain (Linux: SIGTERM lets a job finish and the container exits 0; Windows: a stock container is killed after about 5 seconds, the control, and an idle real runner drains), the persistent class, limits, class isolation, exit 80 with no hot loop, and the entrypoint on cimg, Alpine and UBI placement.sh, drain.sh, persistent.sh, limits.sh, network.sh, exit80.sh, bats, and the Test-*.ps1 equivalents
data.tests#Tests: ci/tests/setup-gate.sh: a table of branches, contexts, parameters, tokens and changed paths, and the flags the gate must print. It also checks that the gate sets exactly the parameters of continue.yml. It needs bash and jq. ci/tests/setup-config.sh: compiles .circleci/config.yml for a table of branches and checks that one setup workflow is left, that the e2e context appears only on main and smr-swarm/*, and that every other branch gets a job without a context. ci/tests/changed-files.sh: runs the script on throwaway repositories (several commits, an unknown base, a shallow clone, one commit of each type against cliff.toml). A pipeline of main or smr-swarm/* started through the API, or an SSH rerun of such a job, is refused by the context restriction: its setup job fails with an authorization error. Start the full suite on another branch with full: true, or push a commit.
data.the-docker-hub-context#The Docker Hub co:
The scalable-machine-runner-dockerhub context holds two variables for publishing the token proxy image (The token proxy image):
Variable Value DOCKERHUB_USERNAME The Docker Hub user (or organization service account) that may push to ccilabs/machine-runner-swarm-proxy DOCKERHUB_TOKEN An access token of that user with read and write on that repository. Never the password Restrict the context to this project and to main, so that no other branch, SSH rerun or API-started pipeline can read the token. Anyone who can push a branch could otherwise print it and push a malicious image under the tag the stack files name. is the organization slug and is 7bbdbb66-6ba8-4f6c-982e-d4fb401ec257:
circleci context restriction create scalable-machine-runner-dockerhub --org --type project --value circleci context restriction create scalable-machine-runner-dockerhub --org --type expression \ --value 'pipeline.git.branch == "main" and not job.ssh.enabled and not (pipeline.config_source starts-with "api")' The flag is --value, and the first command is needed: an expression alone does not tie the context to this project. The live context has both restrictions. The CLI cannot list them: check the web app (Organization Settings, Contexts), or the API, where the id is in the output of circleci context list --org :
curl --header "circle-token: ${CIRCLECI_TOKEN}" https://circleci.com/api/v2/context//restrictions It must show one project and one expression restriction.
Only jobs that run on main carry the context (the publish variants of the image jobs, proxy-image-publish, proxy-image-edge and release). Until both values exist, a pipeline that is not the production main pushes nothing and stays green: the image jobs build and test, then print NOT PUSHED with the reason, and the release builds its bundle without creating the release. On the production main the missing values fail those jobs (Publishing fails closed on main).
data.the-e2e-context-and-smr-swarm#The e2e co:
The scalable-machine-runner-e2e context holds the runner tokens, and its restriction names main and every branch that starts with smr-swarm/ (Secrets and public logs). The configuration of a job comes from its own branch, so anyone who can push smr-swarm/anything can change .circleci/ there, print the tokens in a public log and read them. That is a deliberate trade while the e2e work lives on its own branch. The maintainers have set the second ruleset (step 3) before the first release. To end the trade:
After the merge, rotate both runner tokens (Maintainer tasks). Any token that a branch could read before is untrusted. Limit the context to main or to exact branch names: change the when of setup-e2e in .circleci/config.yml, the expression restriction of the context, eligible in ci/setup-gate.sh, and the rows of ci/tests/setup-gate.sh and ci/tests/setup-config.sh. Restrict who can create the branches with a second ruleset: target smr-swarm/**, Restrict creations and Restrict updates, bypass list of the maintainers only. Until the context is limited to main, this ruleset keeps the tokens with the maintainers.
data.troubleshooting#Troubleshooting: Symptom Cause and fix setup says an e2e group is skipped The context is missing or lacks the secret. The log names the absent token. Only setup-e2e (main and smr-swarm/*) has the context setup of main or smr-swarm/* fails with an authorization error The context’s expression restriction refused an API-started pipeline or an SSH rerun. Push a commit, or rerun without SSH e2e-*-b1 stays queued and the host job failed The sweep could not claim it (token rejected, or Docker Hub unreachable). Cancel the workflow in the UI to release the serial-group lock Host fails with “token was rejected (401)” Rotate the token (Maintainer tasks) Host fails with “container for probe bN exited without evidence” The runner idled out without claiming the probe, or claimed another job on the e2e class. Check the probe job and e2e/logs/service.log in the artifacts Probe fails “not claimed by the e2e host of workflow …” A runner outside this workflow holds the e2e token, or the host’s sweeper claimed the probe after a failure. A cancelled workflow also releases the lock at once, and the idle service of the cancelled host can claim the next pipeline’s B1. Check that Auto-cancel redundant workflows is off (Secrets and public logs), and rerun lint-stack, a linux-swarm job or release fails with config machine-runner-swarm-... is stale A file that a Swarm config carries changed and the name did not. Run ci/config-names.sh --write and commit lint-shell fails with SC2154 on an uppercase variable .shellcheckrc enables check-unassigned-uppercase. Assign the variable (${NAME:-}) or add # shellcheck disable=SC2154 with the reason Runner log says failed to remove working directory or could not clean up task, with permission denied Only when CIRCLECI_RUNNER_CLEANUP_WORK_DIR is true on a Linux service (the default is false). See Error: failed to remove working directory Test-StopHandling.ps1 or the e2e fails with exit code 3221225786 A container that ran a job was ended about 5 seconds after an outside stop. The e2e never stops a busy container: look for what stopped the stack (a second pipeline, an early cleanup). Check reports/stop-*.txt

A branch pusher chooses the configuration that a job of that branch runs, so what matters is which job holds which secret. A job without a context sees none of these values:

data.what-is-tested#What is tested: This is the short answer for users and reviewers. A claim in the user documentation that this section does not support is an overclaim: report it.
data.when-things-run-and-the-setup-gate#When:
A setup job reads the changed files and decides which suites a pipeline runs. A change runs the suites that read what it changed. A push to main that would make a release runs everything.
Push Setup workflow Runs any branch except main and smr-swarm/* setup-plain, no context lint, docs-site-build, and each suite whose files changed. Never e2e or release the same, with the pipeline parameter full: true setup-plain, no context every suite, the Server 2025 jobs and linux-mixed-arch. Never e2e or release smr-swarm/* setup-e2e, with the e2e context as any branch, plus e2e-linux and e2e-windows for the tokens present and the files changed. No Server 2025 jobs, no linux-mixed-arch main, a commit of the push would make a release setup-e2e every suite, full-suite, and the e2e groups for the tokens present. With both tokens: release and proxy-image-edge too main, no commit of the push would make a release setup-e2e as a branch: suites and e2e groups by changed files. No release, no proxy-image-edge, no full-suite any push that changes documentation only (below) the same lint and docs-site-build only the schedule of the security scan setup-scan, no context the workflow security-scan only a tag none nothing: the setup job has no tag filter, so CircleCI runs no job setup-e2e runs when the branch is main or starts with smr-swarm/. Its setup job has the scalable-machine-runner-e2e context, which holds the runner tokens. setup-plain runs on every other branch and has no context, so no token exists in a job of another branch. setup-scan runs only when security-scan is true, on any branch, and never has the context. An e2e group is added only when the job sees its token (E2E_RUNNER_TOKEN_LINUX, E2E_RUNNER_TOKEN_WINDOWS). Without the context the pipeline still runs lint, builds and local tests, and stays green.
ci/setup-gate.sh makes the decision. The setup job passes --e2e true (the job with the context) or --e2e false (the plain job, which never enables e2e), the full parameter, the changed files and whether a commit would release.

Each suite has a parameter and a list of paths. It runs when a changed path is in its list, when the push is a release or has full: true, or when the changed files are not known.

A change to .circleci/, ci/setup-gate.sh, ci/changed-files.sh or .gitattributes runs every suite, because the pipeline definition changed. Other paths. A path in no list (a lint configuration, examples/, ci/release.sh) runs lint only. Not known. The first build of a branch or a pipeline started through the API runs every suite. On main it runs everything. full-suite. The Server 2025 jobs (windows-swarm-ltsc2025, proxy-image-windows-ltsc2025) and linux-mixed-arch run only on a release push to main and with full: true. Which commits. On a branch: everything since the merge base with origin/main. On main: everything since the commit of the build that ran before (pipeline.git.base_revision). data.why-the-gate-is-in-the-setup-phase#Why t: A guard job that runs circleci-agent step halt is not enough. The probe jobs target a self-hosted runner class and queue until a runner claims them, which can take days. Halting a guard job ends only that job, so the probes would still be scheduled. The decision has to happen before the e2e jobs are compiled into the workflow. The setup job calls the continuation API itself instead of using the circleci/continuation orb, because the orb prints the request body, and the continuation key with it, into a public log.
data.windows#Windows:
e2e-windows-2022 (job group, serial-group /e2e-windows) e2e-windows-2022-host (A), -b1, -b2, -b3 e2e-windows-2025 (the same group on Server 2025, requires e2e-windows-2022) The host (ci/E2E-Host.ps1) has the same shape, with one service and three probes:
Prepare pulls the stock image, runs windows\Setup.ps1 -InitSwarm -AdvertiseAddr, and deploys the shipped stack with no runner replicas until the distributor has installed the runner and Git. It removes the stack again, and the volume stays. Run takes the shipped windows/stack/runners.yaml as text, replaces ltsc2022 with the host’s tag, layers an override on it (one replica of windows-default on the stock image, an idle timeout, the evidence mount) and deploys with --resolve-image never (the image is local). The secret windows-default-token is built from E2E_RUNNER_TOKEN_WINDOWS and only the token proxy mounts it. The windows/amd64 proxy of proxy-test is installed by the distributor from a local mirror (C:\e2e-proxy, a bind mount). Each probe’s MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_INSTANCE_ID must equal the Swarm task ID of its container (the stack sets it to {{.Task.ID}}), and the computer name must be that container’s ID. The probes plant residue in the user profile, %TEMP%, C:\ProgramData, C:\Users\Public, the registry (HKLM:\SOFTWARE\SwarmE2E) and the machine environment (SWARM_TEST_E2E). Windows has no step-down, so the probe records, and does not assert, whether the job can read the token. Normal flow only: every probe’s job finishes by itself, and every container exits 0. The e2e does not stop a busy container, because on stock Server Core that kills the job after about 5 seconds (Stop a busy Windows container).
data.windows-jobs#Windows jobs:
windows-swarm runs on the stock Server Core image. There is no entrypoint script: the runner (circleci-runner.exe machine --config C:\ProgramData\Docker\secrets\circleci_runner_config.yaml) is the container’s main process, and the runner and portable Git come from the read-only mounts C:\machine-runner-swarm and C:\Program Files\Git of the volume runner-bin, which the stack’s distributor fills. Steps:
Engine check: docker info must report OSType windows. Windows PowerShell 5.1 unit tests (Invoke-UnitTests.ps1, Pester 5.7.1). The image registers both a Nuget and a PSGallery repository, so modules install with -Repository PSGallery. docker pull of the stock image, then windows\Setup.ps1 -InitSwarm -AdvertiseAddr (swarm init and the machine-runner-swarm.windows-ltsc* node labels). Pulling comes first because the network is down for a few seconds after the swarm is created. Test-Install.ps1 then deploys the shipped stack with no runner replicas, so the distributor installs the runner and Git from the real manifest, and checks the result. The volume stays for the next tests. The tests Test-Injection.ps1 -Online, Test-Ephemerality.ps1, Test-Exit80.ps1, Test-Placement.ps1, Test-StopHandling.ps1 -Online, Test-Persistent.ps1 and Test-Distributor.ps1. Each prints CHECK lines and one RESULT line, and exits 0 only on a pass. ci\Invoke-Test.ps1 runs each in a child PowerShell, checks its exit code (a CircleCI PowerShell step does not stop on a failed native command by itself), and keeps the full output as an ASCII report under reports/ (artifacts). Tee-Object would write UTF-16 and miss what a script writes with [Console]::Out.

data: Thank you for helping to improve machine runner swarm, a CircleCI Labs project. Field engineers review issues and pull requests on a best-effort basis, with no SLA. Report a security problem by email, not in an issue (SECURITY.md).
data.commit-messages#Commit messages:
Use Conventional Commits: type(scope): summary. The release job reads these messages to choose the version and write the release notes. Keep each commit small and atomic.
Type Use for feat A new capability, or a changed stack-file contract fix A bug fix docs Documentation only test Tests only ci The CircleCI pipeline chore Maintenance with no user-visible change refactor, perf Code changes that keep behavior, or improve speed Common scopes are linux, windows, docs, readme, and ci.
A breaking change appears first in the release notes, and while the version is 0.x it raises the minor number. Mark it in one of two ways, and write what the user has to change:
Add ! after the type or scope: feat(linux)!: rename the persistent service.
Add a BREAKING CHANGE: footer:
feat(linux): rename the persistent service BREAKING CHANGE: the service is now linux-persistent. Rename it in your stack file.
data.development#Development:
Requirements: Docker with privileged containers for the Linux suite, bash, and PowerShell 7 for the Windows unit tests.
linux/tests/run-all.sh linux/tests/run-all.sh token drain linux/tests/stack-config.sh pwsh -File windows/tests/Invoke-UnitTests.ps1 -InstallModules The commands run the whole Linux suite, a subset, the stack file contract (no daemon needed), and the Windows unit tests (PSScriptAnalyzer and Pester).
The Linux tests run a Swarm inside docker:dind containers, so your own Docker engine never enters Swarm mode. Each test prints RESULT lines and exits 0 when it passes. CI runs the Windows Swarm tests on Windows Server 2022 and 2025. CI/CD lists the pipeline and every lint command.
CI runs the Linux groups as four parallel jobs, each with its own list (linux-swarm in .circleci/continue.yml). Add a new test to all in run-all.sh and to one of those lists: lint-circleci fails when a group is in no list or in two (Linux jobs without a token).
Test What it checks stack-config.sh docker stack config for every combination of stack files, and the Swarm config names helper.sh setup.sh --swarm-init, --secret and --deploy on a fresh Docker-in-Docker daemon ephemerality.sh A new container for every job and no residue, with docker run --restart always as the negative control exit80.sh The restart delay, no hot loop, and the exit codes 80 and 1 of the real runner token.sh What a job can read in the default class and in the hardened class task.sh The real runner runs tasks as the job user, also with CIRCLECI_RUNNER_CLEANUP_WORK_DIR=true and as a persistent runner proxy.sh The token proxy image in a Swarm, in front of the real runner placement.sh Placement on a manager and a worker, and docker-build.yaml distributor.sh The runner-distributor service: install, upgrade, rollback, pins, floating versions, pruning, a tampered binary, a wrong SHA-256, and CircleCI’s real manifest. Needs network access persistent.sh Continuous mode and persistent.yaml microvm.sh The microVM add-on with Kata Containers. Skipped without /dev/kvm. Downloads Kata (about 1 GB) unless SWARM_TEST_KATA_DIR or SWARM_TEST_KATA_TARBALL points at a copy. Not part of run-all.sh drain.sh SIGTERM during a job: the job finishes limits.sh init, ulimits, pids, memory, CPU, reservations, and the capability sets network.sh Network isolation between classes, and between the replicas of a class container-mode.sh The prototype container agent in a Swarm, against a fake API. Needs the Go and pause images bats/run.sh The entrypoint unit tests on cimg/base, Alpine, and UBI minimal The suite needs no installed runner: the distributor of the shipped stack installs one from a small HTTP mirror in the harness. Most tests publish fake-runner.sh, and task.sh, token.sh, exit80.sh, placement.sh, distributor.sh and the idle case of drain.sh publish the real runner binary, which the harness downloads once and checks against the SHA-256 of CircleCI’s manifest.
Three variables change the setup: SWARM_TEST_DIND_IMAGE sets the Docker-in-Docker image, SWARM_TEST_CACHE sets the directory that caches the real runner binary (~/.cache/swarm-tests by default), and SWARM_TEST_KEEP=1 keeps the containers for debugging.
The Windows tests in windows/tests print CHECK PASS|FAIL lines and one RESULT line, and exit 0 only when every check passes. Invoke-UnitTests.ps1 runs the Pester tests on any system with PowerShell 7. The Test-*.ps1 scripts (Injection, Ephemerality, Exit80, Placement, StopHandling, Install, Distributor and Persistent) need a Windows host with Docker in Windows-container mode and no runner token. Each script’s header says what it checks. Test-Injection.ps1 -Online and Test-StopHandling.ps1 -Online use the real runner.
data.documentation-checks#Documentation check:
Documentation follows the CircleCI docs style: sentence-case headings, active voice, no contractions, and short sentences. Every docs/*.md page has front matter with page-title, page-audience, and page-description. CI checks the relative links and the Mermaid diagrams. To run the same checks locally:
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/input" -w /input lycheeverse/lychee:0.24.2 --config lychee.toml './**/*.md' docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/workdir" davidanson/markdownlint-cli2:v0.18.1 '**/*.md'
data.license#License: By contributing, you agree that your contributions are licensed under the MIT license.
data.opening-a-pull-request#Opening a pull re:
Before you open a pull request:
Discuss large changes in an issue first. Run the tests for the platform you changed (Development). Update docs/ when you change a variable, label, secret, port, or default. Write every commit message, and the pull request title, as a Conventional Commit (Commit messages). The release notes are generated from them, so there is no changelog entry to add. Check that the diff has no tokens, host names, or customer or vendor names. The repository is public. A pull request from a fork gets no CI. The project builds no forked pull request and passes no secret to one (Secrets and public logs). A maintainer reads the change and, to run CI, pushes its commits to a branch of the project by hand. Never push or mirror an outside branch to main or to a branch named smr-swarm/*: those names get the e2e runner tokens and, on main, the publishing contexts, and a job takes its configuration from its own branch.
A pull request that changes only documentation (docs/, site/, Markdown files) runs the lint jobs and the docs site build, and skips the builds and the Swarm tests (Documentation-only changes).
Use the pull request template. Maintainers choose the merge method: a squash merge turns the pull request title into the commit message on main, and a merge commit or rebase keeps your commits (Merge method).
data.pinned-versions-and-releases#Pinned vers:
Renovate opens a pull request every Monday for the pinned versions: images and digests, the tools that CI downloads, the Go toolchain and the docs theme (renovate.json; Pinned versions lists what it covers). A pull request with the label checksum changes a version that is pinned with a SHA-256 value. Renovate cannot compute the value, so replace it in the same branch before you merge.
Pin images by tag and digest, and a new download by its version and checksum together, with a # renovate: comment above the version. The default runner version is pinned in three files that must stay equal (linux/stack/runners.yaml, linux/stack/microvm.yaml and windows/stack/runners.yaml), and each release bumps it (how). The pinned Git and 7-Zip versions and their SHA-256 values are in windows/stack/runner-distributor.ps1, and a change of the script needs ci/config-names.sh --write.
Nobody tags a release or edits a changelog: a CircleCI job on main reads the Conventional Commits, and a push with only docs, test, ci, chore, style, or refactor commits makes no release (Releasing, CHANGELOG.md).
data.reporting-a-bug#Reporting a bug:
Search the existing issues first, and check that you use the latest release. Then open a new issue with the bug template. Include:
The release or commit, and the runner version. On Linux, run docker run --rm -v runners_runner-bin:/v:ro alpine cat /v/current/VERSION on the node. On Windows, run docker service logs --tail 100 runners_runner-distributor-windows. The operating system of the node and the Docker Engine version. The output of docker service ps --no-trunc runners_ and docker service logs --tail 100 runners_. Remove tokens, runner config files, and internal host names from everything you paste.
data.requesting-a-feature#Requesting a featur: Open an issue with the feature request template. Describe the problem, and name the platform and the files it affects. For problems in the CircleCI platform or the runner agent, contact CircleCI support instead.
data.swarm-config-names#Swarm config names: The entrypoint and distributor scripts reach the nodes as Swarm configs. A Swarm config cannot change, and a service keeps the old file when the name stays, so the name of each config in the stack files carries the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of its file. After you change linux/stack/circleci-runner-entrypoint, linux/stack/runner-distributor.sh, windows/runner-distributor.ps1, or a file of linux/stack/container-agent, run ci/config-names.sh --write and commit the new names with the change. lint-stack, linux/tests/stack-config.sh and the release job fail on a stale name.

data:
This page is for maintainers. A CircleCI job makes every release when a change is merged to main. Nobody tags a release by hand, edits a changelog, or pushes a release commit. The job creates the tag through the GitHub API.
Version and notes rules: cliff.toml The job: release in the ci workflow of .circleci/continue.yml, and ci/release.sh How users check a release: Verify a release
data.bump-the-runner-version#Bump the runner:
The stack files pin one exact runner version by default: MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_VERSION: ${MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_VERSION:-3.1.13} in the distributor settings of linux/stack/runners.yaml and windows/stack/runners.yaml, and in x-env of linux/stack/microvm.yaml. It is the newest version that CI tests (STACK_RUNNER_PIN in linux/tests/lib.sh), so a release carries the pin that CI tested. Bump it in a commit before each release:
Pick the newest version in the manifest that has linux amd64, arm64, ppc64le, s390x and windows amd64, arm64. List versions with jq -r '.releases | keys[]' manifest.json and check .releases[""]. Read the runner changelog. In one commit, change the default of MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_VERSION in all three stack files. Change the default of MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_SHA256 to the tarball SHA-256 values of that version (from the release’s checksums.txt or the manifest), comma-separated: linux amd64, arm64, ppc64le, s390x in linux/stack/runners.yaml and linux/stack/microvm.yaml, and windows amd64, arm64 in windows/stack/runners.yaml. Commit it as feat(runner): pin 3.1.14 by default for a new minor or patch that users should get, or fix(runner): ... for a fix, so that git-cliff makes a release. Let CI run. Update the docs examples (docs/operations.md uses 3.1.12 and 3.1.13) only when you want them to move. The version must be equal in every file: linux/tests/stack-config.sh fails when it differs. The release job (check_runner_pin in ci/release.sh) fails when the version is not in the manifest for every platform, or when a default SHA-256 list does not match the manifest. A user gets the new runner by deploying the new release. A user who sets the variable keeps what they set.
data.check-the-settings#Check the settings:
Read the GitHub settings back with the API. The first command lists the rules that apply to main (it must include pull_request, non_fast_forward, deletion and required_status_checks). The second and third show the bypass list of a ruleset, which must be empty for main:
gh api repos/CircleCI-Labs/machine-runner-swarm/rules/branches/main --jq '.[].type' gh api repos/CircleCI-Labs/machine-runner-swarm/rulesets --jq '.[] | "\(.id) \(.name) \(.enforcement)"' gh api repos/CircleCI-Labs/machine-runner-swarm/rulesets/ --jq '{conditions, bypass_actors, rules: [.rules[].type]}' The ruleset of smr-swarm/** must show creation and update. The CLI cannot list context restrictions, so read them from the API for each of the five contexts and compare them with the table. Find a context id with circleci context list --org :
curl -s --header "circle-token: ${CIRCLECI_TOKEN}" https://circleci.com/api/v2/context//restrictions The project settings are in the web app (Project Settings, then Advanced), and the Docker Hub token scope is in the account’s security settings. Keep the output with the release pull request.
data.enable-publishing#Enable publishing:
Until you do this, the release job runs every step except the last and stays green on a project with no e2e tokens. It prints publishing skipped: GITHUB_TOKEN is not set in context scalable-machine-runner-release and keeps the version, notes, bundles and signature as job artifacts. On the production main (both e2e tokens present) it fails with the same message.
Create a fine-grained personal access token with the resource owner CircleCI-Labs, only this repository, and the repository permission Contents: Read and write. Nothing else is needed, because gh release create makes the tag and the release. The token expires, so note the date to rotate it. A GitHub App installation token expires after one hour, so it does not fit a context variable.
In the CircleCI organization settings, create the context scalable-machine-runner-release and add the variable GITHUB_TOKEN with the token.
Restrict the context to this project, and add an expression restriction so that only pipelines of main can use it, not an SSH rerun that could print the token and not an API pipeline (which can name any branch and may bring its own config):
pipeline.git.branch == "main" and not job.ssh.enabled and not (pipeline.config_source starts-with "api") With the CLI, where is 7bbdbb66-6ba8-4f6c-982e-d4fb401ec257:
circleci context restriction create scalable-machine-runner-release --org --type project --value circleci context restriction create scalable-machine-runner-release --org --type expression \ --value 'pipeline.git.branch == "main" and not job.ssh.enabled and not (pipeline.config_source starts-with "api")' In the organization’s advanced settings, leave pipelines with an unversioned config off.
In the project settings (Advanced), keep Build forked pull requests and Pass secrets to builds from forked pull requests off.
Protect main with the ruleset in A ruleset for main: a pull request required, no force push, no bypass, and the check ci. Whoever can change .circleci/ or ci/release.sh on main controls what runs with the token. What the release trust depends on lists every setting that the signature relies on.
The docs site, its pull request comment and the weekly security scan have their own contexts (What a maintainer creates once). Do not reuse this token for them: it can publish releases. The next release run on main publishes. To check before then, read the release job log for publishing skipped.
data.how-the-signature-works#How the signatur:
The job gets an OIDC token with circleci run oidc get --claims '{"aud":"sigstore"}' --root-issuer. The audience sigstore and the issuer https://oidc.circleci.com are what the public Sigstore certificate authority (Fulcio) accepts for CircleCI. cosign sign-blob swaps the token for a short-lived certificate, signs SHA256SUMS and records the signature in the public Rekor log. No key is kept.
The certificate identity is https://circleci.com/api/v2/projects//pipeline-definitions/. It is the same for every branch, and a job of any branch can get an OIDC token with no context, so the identity alone does not prove that main signed. The source repository ref does: the certificate extension 1.3.6.1.4.1.57264.1.14, which Fulcio fills from the vcs-ref claim. It is refs/heads/main for a release and refs/heads/ for any other branch.
cosign has flags for the GitHub extensions only, so ci/tools.sh reads the certificate itself (signed_only_on, tested by ci/tests/signature-ref.sh):
ci/release.sh runs cosign verify-blob on SHA256SUMS, then checks that the certificate names refs/heads/main. The job stops if it does not. ci/proxy-image.sh does the same for every digest of the token proxy image, right after signing and again in the release job before the release tags. It reads every signature of the digest (cosign download signature): one signature of a feature branch next to one of main fails the check. To check the ref by hand, after cosign verify-blob printed Verified OK, run this. The hex string is the OID followed by refs/heads/main, so it matches the whole value:
jq -r '.verificationMaterial | (.certificate // .x509CertificateChain.certificates[0]).rawBytes' SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json | base64 -d \ | od -An -v -tx1 | tr -d ' \n' | grep -Eq '^([0-9a-f]{2})*2b0601040183bf30010e0411(0c|13)0f726566732f68656164732f6d61696e' \ && echo "signed for refs/heads/main" || echo "NOT signed for refs/heads/main: do not use this release" CircleCI documents OIDC tokens for jobs that use a context. In a test on 2026-10-13, circleci run oidc get also worked in a job without one, which is why the ref and not the identity decides.
data.make-a-release#Make a release:
Bump the runner pin in a commit before the release (Bump the runner version), for example feat(runner): pin by default.
Preview the next version and its notes in a clone with the tags:
git cliff --bumped-version git cliff --unreleased --tag "$(git cliff --bumped-version)" --strip header Merge the pull request to main. The pipeline runs every test, then the release job publishes.
If a job fails, fix it and use Rerun workflow from failed in CircleCI.
Check the release:
gh release view --repo CircleCI-Labs/machine-runner-swarm Then verify the bundle and the image, including the ref, as a user does (Verify a release).
A push with only docs, test, ci, chore, style, refactor or build commits makes no release. The job ends green with Nothing to release since vX.Y.Z.
data.merge-method#Merge method:
The notes come from the commits on main, so the merge method decides what they show.
Merge commit or rebase and merge. Every commit of the pull request gets its own entry, so use it for small, atomic Conventional Commits (Commit messages). The GitHub merge commit is not a Conventional Commit, so the notes ignore it. Squash and merge. The pull request becomes one commit with its title as the message, and one entry that links to the pull request. Write the title as a Conventional Commit. A pull request that mixes a feat and a fix loses one of them. Mark a breaking change with ! or a BREAKING CHANGE: footer, in a commit message or in the title of a squashed pull request.
data.move-the-project-to-circleci-public#Move: Replace the Labs wording in the banner and the Support section of README.md, SECURITY.md, the support paragraph at the top of CONTRIBUTING.md, .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml, and .github/CODEOWNERS. Decide the license, because CircleCI runner repositories use Apache-2.0 and this one uses MIT.
data.pinned-tools#Pinned tools:
ci/release.sh install-tools installs the tools of the job. Each download is checked against a SHA-256 value in the script (cosign and crane are in ci/tools.sh), and the job image is pinned by digest. Each tool has its version and SHA-256 value in two variables, with a # renovate: comment above the version.
Tool Version Source of the SHA-256 value git-cliff 2.14.2 The .sha512 file of the release, and a local sha256sum cosign 3.1.3 cosign_checksums.txt of the release crane 0.22.1 checksums.txt of the release (the Linux x86_64 archive) gh 2.102.0 gh_2.102.0_checksums.txt of the release Go 1.27.2 The download page of go.dev, next to the archive cimg/base 2026.10 The digest in .circleci/continue.yml Renovate opens a pull request that changes the version only. It has the label checksum and fails on the checksum until you replace the SHA-256 value in the same branch. To update a tool by hand, change its version and SHA-256 value together in install_tools (cosign and crane: in ci/tools.sh), then follow Try it locally. To update the job image, follow Pinned versions. A Renovate pull request for Go also moves the golang and cimg/go images, so the release proxy binaries use the same Go as proxy-test.
data.release-notes#Release notes: git-cliff writes the notes for the GitHub release: breaking changes first, then features, bug fixes, performance changes and reverts. The (#123) that GitHub adds to a squash merge title links to the pull request, and an entry without one links to its commit. CHANGELOG.md in the repository only points to GitHub Releases. The release bundle holds a generated CHANGELOG.md with every release.
data.rerun-and-recovery#Rerun and recovery:
Rerunning is safe. Before it publishes, the job looks for a release tag at its commit, and it never creates a second release. Rerunning a pipeline from before a later release releases nothing.
Situation What to do The release job failed before it published Rerun the job. It computes the same version An asset of an existing release is missing Rerun the job. It uploads all assets again with --clobber A tag exists at another commit Stop. Somebody created vX.Y.Z by hand, or an older release was moved. Compare git rev-parse vX.Y.Z with the commit of the pipeline. Delete the wrong tag and release with gh release delete vX.Y.Z --cleanup-tag, then rerun the job This commit is already part of vX.Y.Z A later commit was already released. The job did nothing The release job shows as skipped A newer pipeline waits for the release lock and will release this change too The Deploys view shows FAILED Read the reason there, fix the cause and rerun the job. It records a new deploy of the same version gh fails with 401 or 403 The token expired or lost its permission. Replace GITHUB_TOKEN in the context and rerun the job A release is wrong Prefer a new release that fixes it. If you delete a release and its tag, the next run makes the same version again
data.rotate-the-e2e-runner-tokens#Rotate the:
Rotate both e2e runner tokens when one may have leaked, and when someone who could read them leaves the project. For each class, create a new token, store it in the context, run one pipeline on main and check that both e2e groups pass, then delete the old token. circleci context secret set prompts for the value in a terminal, so the token stays out of the shell history:
circleci runner token create cci-labs/scalable-machine-runner-e2e-linux --nickname ci-YYYYMM circleci context secret set scalable-machine-runner-e2e --org --name E2E_RUNNER_TOKEN_LINUX circleci runner token create cci-labs/scalable-machine-runner-e2e-windows --nickname ci-YYYYMM circleci context secret set scalable-machine-runner-e2e --org --name E2E_RUNNER_TOKEN_WINDOWS circleci runner token list --resource-class cci-labs/scalable-machine-runner-e2e-linux circleci runner token list --resource-class cci-labs/scalable-machine-runner-e2e-windows circleci runner token delete
data.tag-pipelines#Tag pipelines:
The project uses the GitHub OAuth integration (project slug gh/CircleCI-Labs/machine-runner-swarm), which has no trigger settings: CircleCI starts a pipeline for every push that GitHub reports, so the tag that the release creates starts one. In it, pipeline.git.tag is the tag, and pipeline.git.branch and CIRCLE_BRANCH are empty.
That pipeline cannot release and runs no job. CircleCI runs no job for a tag unless the job has a tag filter, and no job in .circleci/ has one. To build for tags, give a job a tag filter on purpose, and keep the release context out of that job.
data.the-signing-rehearsal#The signing rehear:
Signing runs for real on main only, so a failure would first show on a merge and leave sha-<12> tags with no release. The job signing-rehearsal runs the same code in every pipeline that is not documentation-only, on any branch, with no context and no secret (ci/proxy-image.sh rehearse):
It pushes a throwaway image to a registry:2 container of the job at localhost:5000. It signs the image against the real Fulcio and Rekor (a brief failure is tried again, three times) and verifies it with verify_signature, the function that main uses, for the ref refs/heads/. It checks that the same signature is refused for another ref, so a check that stopped looking at the ref turns the pipeline red. Each rehearsal adds an entry to the public Rekor log with the project, branch and commit. The release requires the job.
data.the-token-proxy-image#The token proxy im:
The token proxy is a published image, ccilabs/machine-runner-swarm-proxy on Docker Hub, not a release asset. One tag is a manifest list for linux/amd64, arm64, ppc64le and s390x, and Windows Server 2022 and 2025 (windows/amd64). There is no windows/arm64 image (install-windows.md).
Event Tags pushed A pull request or a branch None: built and tested only A merge to main sha-<12 characters of the commit>, by proxy-image-publish The same merge, after the four linux-swarm jobs and every e2e group pass edge, by proxy-image-edge, the last job of the pipeline. It stays put when a newer commit is on main A release (ci/release.sh) X.Y.Z (immutable), X.Y, X and latest, on the digest of that commit’s sha-<12> image. Nothing is rebuilt The stack files of a checkout default to latest, so only the release job changes what a checkout deploys, and it runs after every test. edge is the newest tested commit, and sha-<12> is one commit that nothing has tested yet. Neither is a default. Before the first release, set MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_PROXY_IMAGE to a sha-<12> or edge tag, or use a release bundle.
X.Y.Z never moves: a release that finds it on another digest stops. X.Y, X and latest move only when the release is the newest of its minor line, its major line and overall. Three helper tags (sha-<12>-linux, sha-<12>-windows-ltsc2022, sha-<12>-windows-ltsc2025) hold parts of the manifest list: do not pull them.
The pipeline builds and runs each image (ci/proxy-image.sh, ci/Build-ProxyImage.ps1, jobs in CI/CD). On main (the pipeline parameter publish), proxy-image-publish joins the helper images with crane index append, tags the list sha-<12>, checks every platform, and signs every digest keyless with the CircleCI OIDC token. The release job pins the digest in the bundle’s stack files (MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_PROXY_IMAGE:-ccilabs/machine-runner-swarm-proxy:@sha256:, in place of :latest), checks the signature, and adds the four release tags.
A checkout keeps latest, which Renovate does not manage. A release bundle carries its own digest, and it is the documented way to install. Users verify the image with cosign (Verify the token proxy image) and must check that the certificate names refs/heads/main (How the signature works).
data.try-it-locally#Try it locally:
Everything except publishing and signing runs on an x86_64 Linux workstation. The first command installs git-cliff, cosign, crane and gh into ~/.local/bin, and Go into ~/.local/go. The second writes the files to /tmp/release and signs and publishes nothing.
ci/release.sh install-tools RELEASE_SKIP_SIGN=1 ci/release.sh To check that the release job requires every job of the workflow, as lint-circleci does, compile the config with every parameter on and read the release entry of workflows.ci.jobs:
circleci config process .circleci/continue.yml \ --pipeline-parameters '{full-suite: true, e2e-linux: true, e2e-windows: true, release: true, publish: true}'
data.versions#Versions:
The project follows Semantic Versioning and starts at 0.x. Tags are vX.Y.Z. git-cliff computes the next version from the Conventional Commits since the last tag. cliff.toml sets initial_tag = "v0.1.0" for a repository with no tag.
Commits since the last release Next version while 0.x A breaking change: type!: or a BREAKING CHANGE: footer Minor, for example 0.2.3 to 0.3.0 feat Minor fix, perf, revert Patch Only docs, test, ci, chore, style, refactor or build No release Not a Conventional Commit, such as a GitHub “Merge pull request” commit Ignored A breaking change never raises the major number: 1.0.0 is a decision for people. To allow it, set breaking_always_bump_major = true and features_always_bump_minor = false in the [bump] section of cliff.toml. The next breaking change then makes 1.0.0.
