docker service logs --tail 30 runners_token-proxy state restored; : N runner(s) have claimed and stay refused means you are done. no state or state lost with running tasks at CircleCI means the runners present are refused (403) until they recycle. Replace the idle ones on a Linux class:
docker service update --force --update-parallelism 0 runners_linux-default A busy Linux replica finishes its job first. On a Windows class, use Replace refused runners on Windows instead.
The image does not change on restart (same tag or digest, unless the tag moved): see Upgrade the token proxy. A stop (this command, a deploy, a node shutdown) lets claims in flight finish, for 8 seconds at most, so a claim CircleCI has answered and that is saved reaches its runner. That is the Linux figure. On Windows, a stop can cut off a claim in flight (A claim whose outcome is unknown).
The start line names one of these states for each class:
state restored. All N latched addresses stay refused, also those DNS does not list yet, until DNS has not listed them for 30 seconds in a row. no state (a first start) with CircleCI reports 0 running tasks. proxy-state was empty and no task of the class runs, so the runners present may claim. no state (a first start) with CircleCI reports M running task(s), or CircleCI does not say how many tasks run. The proxy cannot tell which runners hold the tasks, so it fails safe and latches every runner present until Swarm replaces it. state lost; ... or no state directory; .... The state file is damaged or removed, or there is no state directory: the same decision for every class, from what CircleCI says. A refused runner gets 403 until it recycles: at its idle timeout (1 hour in the shipped files) or at once with the command above. A 401 and a 403 on a claim behave the same in the runner: it keeps its container and claims again every 5 seconds.
data.roll-back#Roll back:
A rollback is a pin of an older version, with its hash policy:
docker service update --env-add MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_VERSION= --env-add MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_SHA256=manifest runners_runner-distributor The distributor keeps the last 3 active versions (about 75 MB each) and never removes the active one. A rollback to a kept version only moves the link: no download, no network. A removed version is downloaded again, with its hash from the manifest or from a list you give. The file history in the volume lists the flips. The next container of every runner service runs the old version, and running jobs are unaffected. Record the same values in deploy/deploy.env.
data.rotate-a-runner-token#Rotate a runner to:
Swarm secrets are immutable: create a second secret and swap it into the service that holds the token. Single-task classes (Linux and Windows) hold it in token-proxy (Windows: token-proxy-windows), one replica, so the swap takes seconds and runners are not touched. Persistent classes hold it in the class service, which updates one replica at a time: a busy replica is replaced after its job ends (up to 5 hours and 5 minutes), so N replicas can take N times that. Raise update_config.parallelism in the stack file, or pass --update-parallelism once (0 replaces every replica at once).
Create a new token in CircleCI. Keep the old one until the swap is complete:
circleci runner token create /linux-default --nickname "linux-default-" Create a secret with a new name, such as linux-default-token-v2:
printf 'New token (hidden): '; stty -echo; IFS= read -r TOKEN; stty echo; echo [ -n "$TOKEN" ] && printf 'api:\n auth_token: %s\n' "$TOKEN" | docker secret create linux-default-token-v2 - unset TOKEN Swap the secret. Single-task class on Linux, in the proxy. Keep the target: the proxy names a class after the file -token, and a new name makes a new class that no runner belongs to:
docker service update \ --secret-rm linux-default-token \ --secret-add source=linux-default-token-v2,target=linux-default-token,uid=65534,gid=65534,mode=0400 \ runners_token-proxy Single-task class on Windows, in token-proxy-windows (Windows secrets have no uid, gid or mode):
docker service update ` --secret-rm windows-default-token ` --secret-add source=windows-default-token-v2,target=windows-default-token ` runners_token-proxy-windows Persistent class on Linux, in the service (on Windows, the same without uid, gid and mode):
docker service update \ --secret-rm linux-persistent-token \ --secret-add source=linux-persistent-token-v2,target=circleci_runner_config.yaml,uid=2000,gid=2000,mode=0400 \ runners_linux-persistent The proxy restarts with its state from proxy-state, so only runners that have not claimed may claim. Recycle runners only when the start log says no state or state lost (Restart the proxy, and on Windows Replace refused runners on Windows), or wait for the idle timeout.
Wait until the update state is completed:
docker service inspect --format '{{.UpdateStatus.State}}' runners_token-proxy Record the new name in your stack file: source: and the entry under the top-level secrets: (for the proxy, the source: of the class under token-proxy). Otherwise a later deploy from the old file reverts the swap.
Revoke the old token and remove the old secret:
circleci runner token list --resource-class /linux-default circleci runner token delete docker secret rm linux-default-token
data.rotate-the-cluster-certificates#Rotate t:
Swarm renews each node certificate before it expires (90 days by default). A node offline longer must leave and join again. After a node was compromised (for example a build job took over a docker-build node), remove it and rotate the CA so its certificate stops working:
docker node rm --force docker swarm ca --rotate Rotate the join tokens too (docker swarm join-token --rotate worker and manager). A compromised node could read the secrets of the tasks that ran on it, and a compromised manager every secret, so also rotate those classes’ tokens (If a token leaked).
data.run-the-cluster#Run the cluster: Reference for production: logs that survive, signals to watch, deploy variables, backups, certificates and failures.
data.run-the-downloads-from-a-mirror#Run the:
A site without a route to CircleCI’s release bucket serves /circleci-runner_linux_.tar.gz for every version the nodes may run from an internal HTTP server. The distributor builds the tarball address from the base URL and version and ignores the manifest’s url fields, so a copy of manifest.json stays unchanged.
Setting Reads manifest.json The mirror must hold An exact pin with its SHA-256 list (the default) Never The pinned version’s tarballs, per node architecture An exact pin of your own with manifest instead of a list Only when the version is not installed yet The tarballs, and manifest.json with an entry for that version A floating value At every start and check interval manifest.json, kept current, and the tarballs it may pick base=https://circleci-binary-releases.s3.amazonaws.com/circleci-runner mkdir -p mirror && curl -fsSL "$base/manifest.json" -o mirror/manifest.json jq -r '.releases | keys[] | select(test("^[0-9]"))' mirror/manifest.json for v in 3.1.12 3.1.13; do mkdir -p "mirror/$v" for arch in amd64 arm64; do curl -fsSL "$base/$v/circleci-runner_linux_$arch.tar.gz" -o "mirror/$v/circleci-runner_linux_$arch.tar.gz" done done Serve mirror and point the distributor at it:
sudo env MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_DOWNLOAD_BASE_URL=https://mirror.example.com/circleci-runner docker stack deploy -c deploy/runners.yaml runners With an exact pin, keep the previous version too, for a rollback. With a floating version, copy its line’s versions and refresh manifest.json to let nodes adopt a release. With current, copy the version it names:
jq -r '.releases as $r | $r.current.linux.amd64.sha256 as $s | $r | to_entries[] | select(.key | test("^[0-9]")) | select(.value.linux.amd64.sha256 == $s) | .key' mirror/manifest.json The distributor uses the wget and CA bundle of the stock Alpine image, so an https mirror needs a certificate from a public authority. Otherwise use an http:// mirror with the SHA-256 list (an exact pin needs a usable list over http, and the default list is enough), or an image of your own for runner-distributor (not tested). MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_ALLOW_HTTP=true accepts http with no list, for a lab (Proxies and certificate authorities).
The mirror replaces the runner download only. Every runner container still downloads its task agent from circleci-binary-releases.s3.amazonaws.com, and every node still pulls alpine from a registry (Does it work on hosts without internet access?).
data.see-what-runs#See what runs:
docker service logs --tail 20 runners_runner-distributor The volume runners_runner-bin exists on every node. On the node to inspect:
docker run --rm -v runners_runner-bin:/v:ro alpine readlink /v/current docker run --rm -v runners_runner-bin:/v:ro alpine cat /v/history docker top | grep circleci-runner The last command names the version directory that a container resolved at start. When a node gets no runner or a download is refused, refer to The runner waits for the distributor, and then exits with code 80.
data.settings-of-the-distributor#Settings of:
Variables of docker stack deploy, for the distributor service only. linux/stack/runners.yaml reads them in x-distributor-env.
Variable Default Effect MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_VERSION The newest version CI tests (3.1.13 in this release) An exact version pins it. 3.1, 3 and current float (the version policy) MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_MAJOR 3 The major version current may adopt MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_CHECK_INTERVAL 24h How often a floating version asks the manifest again, and how often a pin’s installed copy is verified. Seconds, or a number with s, m, h or d MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_DOWNLOAD_BASE_URL https://circleci-binary-releases.s3.amazonaws.com/circleci-runner Where manifest.json and the tarballs are (mirror). Must be https://, unless a SHA-256 list is set MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_SHA256 The four tarball SHA-256 values of the pinned version (amd64, arm64, ppc64le, s390x) A comma-separated list for an exact pin, covering every architecture of your nodes. The distributor installs nothing else, whatever the manifest says. A version of your own needs its own values (the checksums.txt of its release) or manifest (the manifest hash is trusted: weaker). A floating value ignores any list (Runner binary integrity on Linux) MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_ALLOW_HTTP Not set true accepts an http:// base without a SHA-256 list. For a lab: the manifest hash then protects nothing against someone on the path The token proxy is an image, not a distributor setting (Upgrade the token proxy). The architectures are those of CircleCI’s manifest (uname -m). Another one stops the distributor with unsupported architecture.
A variable must reach every docker stack deploy, because a deploy without it sets the default again: keep them in a file. For a try, pass one with env, because sudo drops the environment:
sudo env MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_VERSION=3.1 docker stack deploy -c deploy/runners.yaml runners sudo env MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_VERSION=3.1 linux/setup.sh --deploy --stack-file deploy/runners.yaml
data.ship-the-logs#Ship the logs:
docker service logs reads only logs of tasks Swarm still holds. Every finished job ends a task, and the task history limit of 2 makes Swarm prune old tasks, so a job log is gone after a few more jobs. The stack files keep logs on the node (local driver on Linux, 3 files of 20 MB; json-file on Windows) and rotate them.
The token proxy logs one line (about 85 bytes) per forwarded claim, a 204 included: about one per idle runner every 5 seconds. With 50 idle runners that is about 70 MB a day, so the 60 MB of the Linux proxy and the 10 MB of the Windows proxy wrap within a day, and the lines that matter after an incident (refused, state restored, released) go first. Ship the proxy log off the node, or raise max-file of token-proxy in your copy of the stack file. To keep logs, choose one:
A logging driver. Change logging: in your copy of every stack file to a shipping driver such as syslog, fluentd or gelf. The stack files set the driver per service, so a default in daemon.json does not apply. docker service logs then fails for these drivers. A log agent on every node. It reads container logs through the Docker API and forwards them. The stack files stay as they are, and docker service logs keeps working.
data.stop-a-busy-windows-container#Stop a bus:
On Linux, a stop lets the running job finish. On Windows, stopping a busy container from outside kills its job after about 5 seconds. The normal flow is unaffected: a job finishes, the runner exits, the container ends cleanly, and Swarm starts a new one.
When Docker stops a container, Windows sends it the shutdown event. The runner turns it into SIGTERM and drains, but on Server Core Windows waits only the registry value WaitToKillServiceTimeout before it ends the processes. The default is 5 seconds, whatever docker stop -t or stop_grace_period says. The container exits with code 3221225786 (0xC000013A) and the job dies with it. These stop containers this way: a rolling update (docker stack deploy, docker service update), docker service scale to a lower number, docker node update --availability drain, docker stack rm, and a restart of the Docker service. Roll out changes while the class is idle, or rerun the interrupted jobs.
Microsoft describes the limit in hcsshim pull request 1416 and Windows-Containers issue 164. It is fixed only in the containerd shim, and Swarm uses the Docker engine runtime. Test-StopHandling.ps1 measures the rule in every CI run with a fake 40 second job.
To find an idle class, use a personal API token (on CircleCI server, set $api to your runner API URL). Update or deploy when running_runner_tasks is 0:
$h = @{ 'Circle-Token' = $env:CIRCLECI_API_TOKEN } $api = 'https://runner.circleci.com' Invoke-RestMethod -Headers $h -Uri "$api/api/v3/runner/tasks/running?resource-class=/windows-default"
data.the-node-of-the-proxy#The node of the pr: Draining the node that runs token-proxy stops the proxy: no claim is possible until it runs again, so patch that node last, in a quiet period (Where the proxy runs, and when it moves). Draining every manager, or the only node that can run the proxy, stops every claim: keep one node undrained for it (the warning in Multi-node clusters).
data.the-version-policy#The version policy:
The runner version is operator-pinned, as for CircleCI’s own runners. The default is an exact pin. A floating value is an opt-in.
MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_VERSION What the nodes run Changes by itself An exact version, 3.1.13 (the default) That version: the newest the CI tests, bumped by each release (how). The stack file carries the SHA-256 of its tarballs Never. Once installed, the distributor makes no request for it 3.1 The newest 3.1.x in CircleCI’s manifest At every MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_CHECK_INTERVAL (default 24 hours) 3 The newest 3.x.y in the manifest At every check interval current CircleCI’s current release, within MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_MAJOR (default 3) At every check interval An exact pin takes the tarball SHA-256 from the stack file, so it asks no manifest. Once verified, each interval it only compares the active binary with its record, and reinstalls if the binary changed. A floating value reads manifest.json at start and every interval. current is matched to a versioned manifest entry by SHA-256 and adopted only within MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_MAJOR; another major logs not adopting it and keeps what is installed. A release reaches every node within one interval, with no redeploy. In a stack file, quote a floating value ("3.1"): YAML reads 3.1 as a number and 3.10 as 3.1.
Floating is weaker. A floating value cannot keep a SHA-256 list, so the distributor ignores the default list and takes each tarball’s SHA-256 from CircleCI’s manifest.json. That file comes from the same bucket as the tarball, so whoever can change one can change both, and the check proves only that the download is whole. Use it only for a class that may run whatever CircleCI releases. It can also bring a runner this release has not been tested with (Compatibility with CircleCI).
data.uninstall#Uninstall:
Remove the stack. Swarm sends SIGTERM to the tasks, so running jobs get the grace period to finish:
docker stack rm runners Remove the secrets (-token of every class you deployed) and the persistent-class volumes:
docker secret rm linux-default-token runner-placeholder-token docker volume rm runners_persistent-home runners_proxy-state The Windows persistent class volume is runners_windows-persistent-cache, and the Windows proxy keeps its state in runners_proxy-state too.
The volume runners_runner-bin holds the runner (and Git on Windows) and stays on every node after docker stack rm. Remove it on every node, on Windows after the last container of the stack is gone:
docker volume rm runners_runner-bin Remove the nodes from the Swarm: docker swarm leave on each worker, then docker swarm leave --force on the last manager. No node has files outside Docker to remove.
data.unlock-a-locked-swarm#Unlock a locked sw:
With autolock (docker swarm update --autolock=true), a manager that restarts cannot read the Raft log until you unlock it. A locked manager answers with Swarm is encrypted and needs to be unlocked before it can be used and takes no part in the quorum. Without a quorum nothing creates replacement tasks, so rebooting managers without unlocking them drains capacity. Plan every manager reboot with its unlock.
docker swarm unlock docker swarm unlock-key docker swarm unlock-key --rotate The first asks for the key on the locked manager. The second prints it, on an unlocked manager. The third makes a new key: run it after anyone who knew the old key leaves, and store the new key outside the cluster.
data.update-the-images#Update the images: Stock and your own images. Change the tag or digest of image in your stack file and deploy. Swarm resolves a tag to a digest at deploy: deploy again to pick up a re-pushed tag. Rebuild your own images on a schedule (for example monthly) and when the base image or a tool changes. The distributor image. runner-distributor runs alpine:3, pinned by digest. Change the digest and deploy. It restarts on every node at once, and no running job is affected. Windows base images. Microsoft republishes the Server Core tags each Patch Tuesday. Pin by digest, rebuild your images on top, and change a Windows service only while its class is idle. For one service: docker service update --image runners_. Record it in your stack file.
data.upgrade-docker-and-the-nodes-in-order#Up:
One node at a time, waiting until the cluster is healthy before the next. Managers first, then workers, and the proxy’s node last (docker service ps runners_token-proxy; Windows: runners_token-proxy-windows). With three managers, one is down at most, so the quorum holds.
Drain the node (Drain a node for patching). On Windows, pause it and wait instead. Upgrade Docker and reboot. Unlock a manager that uses autolock. Return it to service (docker node update --availability active ). docker node ls must show it Ready, and a manager Reachable or Leader. After the proxy node, check the proxy log: the start line must say state restored. no state means the proxy moved or lost its volume, and runners are refused until they recycle (Restart the proxy). Leave mixed Docker versions only for the length of the upgrade. The runner upgrades separately, with no stop.
data.upgrade-the-runner-and-images#Upgrade th:
Swarm replaces containers one at a time (order: stop-first, parallelism: 1). A busy replica gets SIGTERM, drains (finishes its job, takes no new one), and is then replaced. An idle replica stops within about 5 seconds with exit code 0. A busy one exits 0 when its job ends, so an update can take as long as your longest job, up to the stop_grace_period of 5 hours and 5 minutes. docker service update waits unless you add --detach.
Goal Section Take a new release Upgrade to a new release Change the runner version only Linux, Windows Change the token proxy Upgrade the token proxy Change job or base images Update the images
data.upgrade-the-runner-on-linux#Upgrade the:
The runner-distributor service is the only way a runner reaches a Linux node and the only place that sets its version. Runner services carry no version and no hash, so an upgrade, pin or rollback changes the distributor only: no runner service restarts and no job is interrupted (The runner distributor on Linux).
On a node, read the active version (See what runs).
Set the new version and its SHA-256 values in deploy/deploy.env. The default is an exact pin that each release bumps, so deploying a newer release is also an upgrade.
Deploy:
sudo ./deploy/deploy.sh Read the distributor log: it names the version it selects and each flip.
Optional: replace the replicas that wait for a job now. An idle replica stops within seconds, a busy one finishes its job first:
docker service update --force runners_linux-default A container resolves the link current once, at start. A running job keeps its version, and the next container (next job) gets the new one. Idle replicas keep the old binary until they claim a job or exit after CIRCLECI_RUNNER_IDLE_TIMEOUT (1 hour). A persistent class runs one container for all jobs: recycle it (Recycle a class).
data.upgrade-the-runner-on-windows#Upgrade th:
The service runner-distributor-windows is the only way a runner and Git reach a Windows node. It works like the Linux distributor: same variables (table), same policy, no version in the runner services. An upgrade, pin or rollback changes the distributor only, so no runner service restarts and no busy job is killed.
It installs into the volume runner-bin (versions\ for the runner, git\ for portable Git) and mounts the links current and git\current read-only at C:\machine-runner-swarm and C:\Program Files\Git. Docker resolves a link when it creates a container, so the next job runs the new version and a running job keeps its directory. The distributor never overwrites a version or removes one in use (Windows cannot replace files a running container uses): it tries again at its next check. During a flip current is missing for a few milliseconds, and a container created then does not start (Swarm retries after the restart delay of 10 seconds). On a new node, runner tasks fail the same way until the first download is done.
Differences from Linux, in x-distributor-env of windows\stack\runners.yaml:
MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_SHA256 defaults to the two values (amd64, arm64) of the pinned version. MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_DOWNLOAD_BASE_URL holds manifest.json and /circleci-runner_windows_.tar.gz. It must be https:// (or file://), unless a SHA-256 list is set. MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_TOOLS_BASE_URL is a directory URL with PortableGit--64-bit.7z.exe (arm64: -arm64.7z.exe) and 7zr.exe, the two downloads the script pins by SHA-256. Without it they come from GitHub. The architecture is amd64 or arm64. CI runs the distributor on amd64 hosts only: arm64 file names and manifest entries are tested, and no Windows arm64 host runs the stack. There is no start-time binary check (no entrypoint script): the distributor compares the active binary with its record at every check and reinstalls it if it changed (Runner binary integrity on Windows). A mirror needs the windows tarballs, the two Git downloads in the tools directory, and manifest.json where the Linux mirror table says. The distributor downloads with PowerShell, so an https mirror needs a certificate the stock Server Core image trusts (not your own authority): otherwise use an http:// mirror with the SHA-256 list, or an image of your own. It reads only HTTPS_PROXY. Set the variables in the shell that runs the deploy, and keep them in a file (Keep the deploy variables in version control). 3.1 trusts the manifest hash (weaker):
$env:MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_VERSION = '3.1' docker stack deploy -c deploy\runners.yaml runners To freeze the nodes or roll back, pin the installed or an older version (no network for a kept version; the last 3 active versions are kept), with the hash policy as on Linux:
docker service update --env-add MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_VERSION=<VERSION> --env-add MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_SHA256=manifest runners_runner-distributor-windows docker service logs runners_runner-distributor-windows shows each flip. On the node, this shows the history and the active version:
docker run --rm --mount type=volume,source=runners_runner-bin,target=C:\v,readonly mcr.microsoft.com/windows/servercore:ltsc2022 powershell -Command "Get-Content C:\v\history; (Get-Item C:\v\current).Target" Waiting replicas keep the old version until they claim a job or exit after CIRCLECI_RUNNER_IDLE_TIMEOUT (1 hour). To replace them at once, force an update only while the class is idle (docker service update --force runners_windows-default).
data.upgrade-the-token-proxy#Upgrade the toke:
The proxy is the image ccilabs/machine-runner-swarm-proxy, read from MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_PROXY_IMAGE by the service token-proxy (Windows: token-proxy-windows). Tags: X.Y.Z (a release, never moves), X.Y, X, latest (the newest release), edge (the newest main-branch commit that passed the end-to-end tests) and sha-<12 characters> (The token proxy image). A release bundle defaults to its own release by tag and digest. A checkout defaults to latest, which only a release moves.
With the release. Deploy the stack files of the new release (Upgrade to a new release of this repository).
Pin a digest. Set ccilabs/machine-runner-swarm-proxy@sha256: in the environment of every deploy (deploy/deploy.env). A digest is the only pin a re-pushed tag cannot move. Read it in the release notes, in the bundle (grep MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_PROXY_IMAGE stack/runners.yaml), or with the command below, and check the signature first (Verify the token proxy image):
docker buildx imagetools inspect ccilabs/machine-runner-swarm-proxy: Change the running service. Swarm stops the old proxy before it starts the new one (a second proxy would allow a second claim). Runners cannot claim for a few seconds, and every runner that has claimed stays refused (Restart the proxy). Record it in deploy/deploy.env. A tag such as latest is resolved to a digest at deploy: deploy again to pick up a newer one.
docker service update --image runners_token-proxy Roll back. Deploy the previous digest or version.
An air-gapped site mirrors the image (this keeps every platform), copies its signature with cosign copy, and sets MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_PROXY_IMAGE=/::
docker buildx imagetools create --tag /: ccilabs/machine-runner-swarm-proxy:
data.upgrade-to-a-new-release-of-this-reposit:
Read the changelog. [BREAKING] entries say what to change.
Merge the differences between your stack file and the new release. Start with the defaults of x-distributor-env: a release bumps the runner version and its MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_SHA256 values together.
Record the new pin (both defaults merged), or your own pin with its two values, in deploy/deploy.env (why).
Deploy with the same -c files and variables as before:
sudo ./deploy/deploy.sh Check the version the distributor selected, then the active one (See what runs):
docker service logs --tail 5 runners_runner-distributor The entrypoint and distributor script are Swarm configs, and a config cannot change, so its name carries the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of its file. A release that changes a file has new names, and the deploy updates the services that use them: runner services one replica at a time, the distributor on every node. If you edit one of these files in your own copy, rename its config after each edit (old prefix plus the first 12 digits of the new hash), or Swarm keeps the old file:
sha256sum linux/stack/circleci-runner-entrypoint | cut -c1-12 sha256sum linux/stack/runner-distributor.sh | cut -c1-12 In a clone of this repository, ci/config-names.sh --write renames the configs of the shipped stack files.
data.verify-a-release-without-internet#Verify: cosign verify-blob and cosign verify fetch the Sigstore trust root over the network by default, and this project has not tested an offline verification. Verify on a host with access (Verify a release), copy the verified files and the images by digest in, and check them on the site with sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS and the digests the verified release names. Recent cosign versions can also verify against a trusted root that you carry in (--trusted-root): test it with a known release first.
data.what-fails-when-it-changes#What fails wh: Change What you see What to do The claim moves to another path The runner logs 401, and the proxy log has no claim from lines for it: the call is forwarded with the placeholder, and CircleCI rejects it Pin the previous runner version (Roll back) A claim with no task gets a 2xx other than 204 Each runner is latched after its first poll: upstream status 200, then this runner has already claimed a task. No runner claims Pin the previous version, and replace the runners (Restart the proxy) scale answers in another shape A proxy that starts with no state logs CircleCI does not say how many tasks run and refuses the runners present until they recycle. A proxy with state is unaffected Open an issue with the log line. Replace the runners, or wait for the idle timeout The runner stops passing its API URL to the task agent, or the agent calls another host The job starts and its steps fail with 401 against CircleCI Pin the previous runner version Before you move to an untested runner version (any floating value included), pin it on one class, run the canary and a real job, read the proxy log, and keep the previous version installed so the rollback needs no network. The runner API hosts nodes must reach are in Egress hosts, with their source, CircleCI’s runner FAQ.
data.what-is-tested#What is tested: The runner version. The exact pin of the stack files, 3.1.13 in this release. The CI runs the real runner binary against a fake API (task.sh, proxy.sh and others), and the end-to-end jobs run real jobs on CircleCI cloud through the proxy, on Linux amd64 and arm64 and Windows Server 2022 and 2025. The distributor test also installs the previous version (3.1.11) for the rollback, and the version CircleCI names as current in the live manifest, and checks its record. Not tested. A real job on a floating version (3.1, 3, current) or any runner version other than the pin. CircleCI server. A runner API on a host other than runner.circleci.com. The task agent is not pinned by this project: the runner downloads the version CircleCI serves, at each container start.
data.what-needs-the-internet#What needs the i:
See What needs internet. The mirror steps are in Run the downloads from a mirror, and the Windows Git downloads come from MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_TOOLS_BASE_URL (Upgrade the runner on Windows).
To mirror the images, copy each with its digest to a registry the nodes reach (this keeps every platform), and change the image: line of every stack file and MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_PROXY_IMAGE. Deploy with --resolve-image never if the manager cannot reach the registry to resolve tags (Registry needs):
docker buildx imagetools create --tag /:
data.what-to-copy-into-the-site#What to copy: For a site that reaches CircleCI through a proxy, or mirrors what it can, copy in the release bundle and SHA256SUMS, the images by digest (the proxy image with its signature via cosign copy), the runner tarballs per node architecture (the pinned version and the one before it, plus manifest.json for a floating version), on Windows the two Git downloads, and for a MicroVM class the Kata tarball.
data.when-the-disk-is-full#When the disk is f:
A node with a full disk fails tasks, with no space left on device in the runner log or in docker stack ps --no-trunc, and Docker commands on it fail. A full manager disk comes first, because Swarm cannot write its log.
Find the node: df -h /var/lib/docker on each, and the ERROR column of docker stack ps runners --no-trunc.
Stop it from claiming jobs. On Linux, drain it. On Windows, pause it (A Windows node):
docker node update --availability drain See what takes the space:
docker system df docker ps -a --size --format '{{.Size}}\t{{.Names}}' | sort -hr | head Free it, cheapest first. docker container prune removes the stopped containers of finished tasks (Swarm does not need them) and no running one. Do not prune volumes:
docker image prune --all --force docker builder prune --force docker container prune --force If the disk is a manager, check that docker node ls and docker service ls answer and the proxy runs (docker service ps runners_token-proxy).
Return the node to service (docker node update --availability active ), set the task history limit if it is not set, and add the scheduled prune.
data.when-the-proxy-cannot-save-its-state#Whe: The proxy saves a runner’s address before it hands the task over. If the save fails (the volume proxy-state is full, read-only or gone), that runner gets 503 and stays refused (403), every other claim gets 503 without reaching CircleCI, and the proxy deletes state.json (so no restart reads a stale state) and reports unhealthy. CircleCI has already allocated that task to the runner, which never runs it: rerun the job if it does not end. Swarm restarts the proxy after 3 failed health checks, and with the state file gone the restart asks CircleCI and refuses every runner of a class with running tasks. Mend the volume (free space, or fix the mount) before or right after: the proxy refuses to start when it cannot write its state directory.
data.where-the-proxy-runs-and-when-it-moves#W:
The proxy runs on a manager by default (node.role == manager). Its state, the addresses of runners that have claimed, is the volume proxy-state of its node.
If the proxy moves, its state is lost. A move happens by itself when its node is down and another manager matches, or by hand when you change the placement. The new node has an empty volume, so the proxy asks CircleCI for each class (Restart the proxy). With running tasks in a class, or no answer, it refuses the existing runners of that class (403) until they recycle. A runner that runs a job is unaffected. Replace the idle ones with docker service update --force --update-parallelism 0 runners_ per Linux class, and on Windows as in Replace refused runners on Windows. No runner can claim twice.
To move the proxy by hand (if no node matches, the service stays pending and no runner can claim):
docker service update --constraint-rm 'node.role == manager' --constraint-add 'node.hostname == ' runners_token-proxy In a cluster, pin the proxy. Label its node and say so at deploy time (Keep the deploy variables in version control):
docker node update --label-add machine-runner-swarm.proxy=true sudo env MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_PROXY_PLACEMENT='node.labels.machine-runner-swarm.proxy == true' docker stack deploy -c deploy/runners.yaml runners The proxy then runs on the labeled node (a manager or a worker), and runner services never run on it, so no job shares a node with the class tokens. On a single node, set no label. If the labeled node dies, the service stays pending until you label another. The labeled node runs no jobs, so size the cluster for that.
Planned work on that node. A reboot keeps the state. Drain the node, patch it and set it active: no runner can claim meanwhile, and running jobs wait for the proxy at the end. Patch this node last (Drain a node for patching). With the default placement, draining moves the proxy with an empty state: pin it first, or accept replacing the refused runners afterwards.
data.where-the-space-goes#Where the space goe: Stopped containers. A job runs in the writable layer of its container, which stays until Swarm prunes the task. A slot keeps its running task and up to task-history-limit finished ones (default 5), so R replicas can hold R times (1 plus the limit) layers. Images. Every tag a job image has had stays until something removes it. docker image prune removes only untagged images. Logs and state. Logs are 3 files of 20 MB per runner on both systems and for the Linux proxy (10 MB for the Windows proxy). A docker-build node keeps the images, volumes and build cache that jobs leave. Each manager keeps the Raft log in /var/lib/docker/swarm.

data:
Each entry gives the symptom, the cause and the fix. After a quickstart, find your symptom here first:
You see Do this runners_linux-default shows 1/2 Run docker service ps --no-trunc runners_linux-default. If the error says insufficient resources, run one replica: sudo docker service scale runners_linux-default=1 (A task stays pending) runners_token-proxy shows 0/1 Run docker service ps --no-trunc runners_token-proxy. A no suitable node error means no node matches its placement: by default it needs a manager, and with MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_PROXY_PLACEMENT it needs an active node with that label. A node with the label machine-runner-swarm.proxy runs no runner services The CLI lists no instance Run docker service logs --tail 50 runners_linux-default, then see The runner log shows 401 and x509 certificate errors The job stays Queued The class name must equal /linux-default, and your plan needs free runner concurrency (Jobs wait while the runners are idle) For anything else, start with the task state and the runner output:
docker stack ps runners --no-trunc docker service logs --tail 100 runners_ For CircleCI guidance shared by all runners, refer to Troubleshoot self-hosted runner.
data.a-service-update-is-paused-or-rolled-bac:
Symptom: docker service update or docker stack deploy stops partway, and this prints paused, rollback_started or rollback_completed (the Message field names the failed task):
docker service inspect --format '{{.UpdateStatus.State}}' runners_ Cause. A new task failed to start, for example exit code 80 after a wrong setting or a missing secret. The stack files set no failure_action, so Swarm pauses at the first failure, and the replicas it did not reach keep the old version.
Fix. Read why the task failed (docker service ps --no-trunc runners_), correct your stack file, and deploy again with the same files. To go back at once:
docker service update --rollback runners_ Refer to Update the images.
data.a-task-stays-pending#A task stays pendin:
Symptom: the ERROR column of docker service ps --no-trunc runners_ shows no suitable node.
Cause. No node satisfies the task.
scheduling constraints not satisfied on N nodes: a label is missing, the OS or architecture differs, or the service needs a worker and the label sits on a manager. insufficient resources on N nodes: the reservations exceed what the matching nodes have free. Reservations equal the limits, so extra replicas wait on purpose. max replicas per node: the SSH add-on runs one replica on each node, because a node has one host-mode port 54782. Fix. Compare the constraints of the service with the labels of the nodes. Then add the label (docker node update --label-add), add nodes, lower replicas, or lower the reservations (Labels and constraints).
docker service inspect --format '{{ json .Spec.TaskTemplate.Placement }}' runners_ docker node inspect --format '{{ .Description.Hostname }} {{ .Spec.Labels }}' $(docker node ls -q)
data.collect-information-for-a-bug-report#Col:
Gather the output of these commands, remove tokens, and open an issue.
docker version docker node ls docker stack ps runners --no-trunc docker service logs --tail 200 runners_ docker service logs --tail 200 runners_token-proxy On Linux, add the runner version (run on the node) and the distributor log:
docker run --rm -v runners_runner-bin:/v:ro alpine cat /v/current/VERSION docker service logs --tail 100 runners_runner-distributor On Windows, add the distributor log:
docker service logs --tail 100 runners_runner-distributor-windows
data.container-exits-with-code-3221225786-aft:
Symptom: a job ends about 5 seconds after a rolling update, scale-down, node drain or docker stop, and docker service ps --no-trunc shows task: non-zero exit (3221225786) (0xC000013A).
Cause. The container was stopped from outside while it ran a job. A job that finishes by itself does not end this way.
Fix. Rerun the interrupted jobs, and change a class only while it is idle (why).
data.error-does-not-match-its-sha-256-record#:
Symptom: the container exits with code 80 and .../versions/3.1.13/bin/circleci-runner does not match its SHA-256 record ...: refusing to start.
Cause. The binary in the volume is not the one the distributor recorded: an incomplete install, a changed volume, or a damaged disk. The entrypoint checks at every start and never runs a different binary (Runner binary integrity on Linux).
Fix. The distributor reinstalls a differing version at its next check. To do it now, force an update, which downloads the version again on every node:
docker service update --force runners_runner-distributor If the binary changes again, find what writes to the volume: a privileged container on the node, or a person with access.
data.error-failed-to-remove-working-directory:
Symptom: every task fails, with failed to remove working directory before starting task or ... while cleaning up task (or could not clean up task), each with permission denied.
Cause. Someone set CIRCLECI_RUNNER_CLEANUP_WORK_DIR to true on a Linux service. The runner (uid 2000) removes its working directory itself, but the job user owns that directory and its files, so even the first task fails. The stack files and the entrypoint default it to false for this reason.
Fix. Set CIRCLECI_RUNNER_CLEANUP_WORK_DIR: "false", or remove the variable so the default applies, and deploy again. A single-task container is discarded after the job, so nothing is lost. In a persistent class, start every job with a step that removes what an earlier job left (Working directory cleanup).
data.error-must-be-owned-by-root-and-not-grou:
Symptom: the container exits with code 80 and .../versions/3.1.13/bin/circleci-runner must be owned by root and not group/world writable.
Cause. The entrypoint refuses a runner that the job user or runner user can replace. The distributor makes the volume files root-owned with mode 0755, so something changed them.
Fix. Set the owner and mode again on the node:
docker run --rm -v runners_runner-bin:/v alpine sh -c 'chown -R 0:0 /v && chmod -R go-w /v'
data.error-the-swarm-does-not-have-a-leader#E:
Symptom: a Swarm command fails with The swarm does not have a leader. It's possible that too few managers are online.
Cause. The managers lost quorum (two of three, or three of five must be online). Running jobs finish, but no replacement task starts, so capacity drops to zero.
Fix. Bring the managers back, starting with the ones stopped last, and check docker node ls on a reachable manager. If the managers are lost for good, recover from one surviving manager:
docker swarm init --force-new-cluster --advertise-addr Refer to Back up the managers, and recover and Managers and quorum.
data.jobs-wait-while-the-runners-are-idle#Job:
Symptom: the runner inventory shows idle runners, and jobs stay queued.
Cause. The inventory shows running tasks only, and queued tasks count against concurrency. A class can sit at the maxConcurrentTasks limit of the resource class (20 by default) or at the runner concurrency of your plan. Jobs for a class with no runner queue forever and hold concurrency.
Fix. Ask the runner API how many tasks wait, and compare it with the replicas. Set RUNNER_API to the runner API of your installation (for CircleCI server).
RUNNER_API=https://runner.circleci.com curl -s -H "Circle-Token: $CIRCLECI_API_TOKEN" "$RUNNER_API/api/v3/runner/tasks?resource-class=/" A count above 0 with idle replicas points at a limit, or at a class name that no service serves. Cancel the tasks of a class with no runners, and ask CircleCI support to raise maxConcurrentTasks (Capacity and concurrency).
data.many-jobs-fail-within-seconds-on-one-nod:
Symptom: jobs of a class fail within seconds or end with no work done, and docker stack ps runners lists many tasks of one node that ended seconds after they started. The node is Ready and the others are fine.
Cause. A Ready node can still fail every job it claims: a full disk, a wrong current link in the runner volume, a bad Docker engine, a clock far off, or a broken route to the registry or CircleCI. A failed task is replaced at once and claims again, so the broken node takes a large share of the jobs. Swarm does not see it, because the node answers its heartbeats.
Fix.
Count the tasks that ended in the last minute for each node. A node far above the others is the one.
docker stack ps runners --format '{{.Node}} {{.CurrentState}}' | grep -E ' (Complete|Failed) [0-9]+ seconds? ago' | cut -d' ' -f1 | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn docker stack ps runners --no-trunc --format '{{.Node}} {{.Name}} {{.CurrentState}} {{.Error}}' | grep '' | head -20 Stop it from taking jobs. On Linux, drain it. On Windows, pause it instead: failing jobs free the node quickly (A Windows node).
docker node update --availability drain Find the cause on the node (Linux):
df -h /var/lib/docker docker run --rm alpine true docker run --rm -v runners_runner-bin:/v:ro alpine ls -l /v/current docker ps -a --filter 'name=runners_' --format '{{.Names}} {{.Status}}' | head timedatectl show -p NTPSynchronized --value Read the newest failed container (docker logs ) and journalctl -u docker -n 100. For a full disk, see Free disk space. A missing current means the distributor has not installed a runner here: The runner waits for the distributor, and then exits with code 80.
Fix the cause and set the node active. If the cause is unclear, run docker swarm leave on it, then docker node rm on a manager, and rebuild it. Rerun the failed jobs.
To see it early, alert on the count in step 1 and keep a canary job for each class.
data.more-linux-symptoms#More Linux symptoms: Symptom Cause and fix Exit code 80 with jobs cannot be stepped down in this image: it needs sudo or util-linux setpriv The image has neither sudo nor util-linux setpriv, or no setpriv and no su to start the runner. A hardened class (MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_JOB_SUDO=false) needs util-linux setpriv even if the image has sudo. Add the packages in a derived image (What an image needs) The distributor logs current is (major ), not 3: not adopting it, or current has SHA-256 , which no versioned release of the manifest has: not adopting it The first: current moved to another major version, and the distributor keeps its version. Read the runner changelog, try it, then set MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_MAJOR or pin the version (Pin a version). The second: the mirror has an old or edited manifest.json. Copy it again, with the tarball of the version current names Every sudo in a job prints unable to send audit message The AUDIT_WRITE capability is dropped. Keep it out of cap_drop (a hardened class keeps it in cap_add) In the hardened class, apt-get install fails with Permission denied, or sudo says the user may not run sudo By design: the class steps jobs down with setpriv --no-new-privs. Build the tools into the image (Bring your own image) docker build fails with Cannot connect to the Docker daemon By design: the class mounts no Docker engine. Use the opt-in class or a daemonless builder (Docker builds) A docker-build job fails with permission denied while trying to connect to the Docker daemon socket The entrypoint adds the job user to the socket’s group but skips group id 0, so a root:root socket gives no access. Give the host socket a group that is not root, normally docker (SocketGroup=docker in the systemd socket unit), check that stat -c '%U:%G %g' /var/run/docker.sock shows a group id above 0, and deploy again no space left on device, Docker commands fail, or the node stops taking jobs Each finished job leaves a stopped container (Swarm keeps five tasks per slot by default), plus images, build cache and logs. Stop the node from taking jobs, free the space and set the history limit (Free disk space). It can look like Many jobs fail within seconds on one node
data.more-swarm-symptoms#More Swarm symptoms: Symptom Cause and fix docker stack deploy fails with secret not found: linux-default-token An external secret does not exist. Every service needs -token, and every single-task runner service (Linux and Windows) also needs runner-placeholder-token. Create it, or delete the service from your copy with its entries under secrets: and networks:. On Windows, runners.yaml needs windows-default-token and runner-placeholder-token, and each add-on file its own -token Swarm is encrypted and needs to be unlocked before it can be used Autolock, and this manager restarted. Run docker swarm unlock and enter the key from docker swarm unlock-key on an unlocked manager (Unlock a locked swarm) This node is not a swarm manager You ran a Swarm command on a worker. Run it on a manager (docker node ls lists them) docker swarm join times out or fails with a connection error The manager is not reachable on its advertised address and port 2377, or listens on loopback only. Open the Inter-node ports, and initialize the swarm with a routable --advertise-addr Jobs queue but no runner claims them The resource_class does not equal /, the class has replicas: 0, or replicas cannot reach CircleCI. Check Runners in the web app, that the tasks run, and Egress hosts A task is rejected with No such image or an authentication error The node cannot pull the image: registry unreachable, image private, or rate limit. Check egress, deploy with --with-registry-auth for a private registry, or use a mirror (Registry needs, What needs the internet) docker service logs prints nothing, or less than you expect Swarm prunes old tasks of a slot with their logs (history limit 5 by default, 2 with the setup helper), and the command reads only the local, json-file and journald drivers. Use docker service ps --no-trunc, docker logs on the node, and Ship the logs A job exits with code 137, or a build fails with fork: Resource temporarily unavailable or Cannot allocate memory 137 is SIGKILL: the kernel kills a job over the memory limit (docker inspect shows OOMKilled: true), or a stop outlasted stop_grace_period. More processes than limits.pids (4096) fails to fork. Raise limits.memory or limits.pids and keep the reservation equal (Size the limits) A job fails with a message that points at an issue with your infrastructure, and its log just stops The runner stopped during the job: a node died or rebooted, a stop from outside (update, scale-down, drain) outlasted the grace period (on Windows, change a class only while it is idle), or an out-of-memory kill. Find the task with docker service ps --no-trunc runners_, then rerun the job: runners do not retry (Node death, Stop a busy Windows container)
data.permission-denied-on-optmachine-runner-s:
Symptom: on RHEL, a replica reports Permission denied for files under /opt/machine-runner-swarm while SELinux is enforcing.
Cause. Untested here: CI does not run on RHEL. Docker normally labels volume files for containers. When it does not, the files keep a type that containers may not read, and a Swarm service mount has no :z option to relabel them.
Fix. Confirm the denial, then label the volume on the node. Files the distributor writes later inherit the label.
sudo ausearch -m avc -ts recent sudo chcon -R -t container_file_t /var/lib/docker/volumes/runners_runner-bin/_data Keep SELinux enforcing. If you needed this, open an issue with the avc line.
data.the-container-restarts-every-10-seconds#:
Symptom: docker service ps lists many tasks of one slot, each with task: non-zero exit (80) or (1), started 10 to 12 seconds apart.
Cause. The runner or the entrypoint exits at start-up on a configuration error. Swarm restarts the container after 10 seconds and never gives up, so the loop runs until you fix the cause. The stack sets no max_attempts, because the runner would then never recover by itself: alert on exit code 80 instead. The log line names the problem:
Log text Cause api.auth_token must be set The secret has an empty token, or the wrong structure runner.name must be set CIRCLECI_RUNNER_NAME is missing runner.name must contain only letters, numbers, .()_-, and spaces Other characters, or more than 64 (long hostname or class name) --runner.mode must be one of "continuous","single-task" CIRCLECI_RUNNER_MODE has another value error parsing config file, or a missing file (exit code 1) The secret is not valid YAML, or not attached with the target circleci_runner_config.yaml circleci-runner-entrypoint: error: ... A missing prerequisite or runner: see the Linux entries Fix. Correct the stack file or the secret and deploy again. To stop the loop meanwhile:
docker service scale runners_=0
data.the-distributor-log-shows-cannot-downloa:
Symptom: runners_runner-distributor logs runner-distributor: cannot download , for manifest.json or a tarball such as /circleci-runner_linux_amd64.tar.gz. The distributor keeps its runner and retries in 5 minutes. Without a runner, the runner containers of the node end as in the entry above.
Cause. The node cannot reach circleci-binary-releases.s3.amazonaws.com or your mirror (egress rule, proxy, DNS, clock), or the file is not on the mirror (for example the pinned version). An https mirror needs a certificate from a public CA, because the distributor uses the CA bundle of the stock Alpine image. A proxy rarely helps: the distributor wget reads only lowercase http_proxy, sends https:// URLs as a plain GET and not CONNECT, and ignores no_proxy.
Fix. Download the same file from the node with the same tool:
docker run --rm alpine wget -q -O /dev/null https://circleci-binary-releases.s3.amazonaws.com/circleci-runner/manifest.json && echo reachable Open the host in Egress hosts, or fix the mirror. A mirror that the node reaches without a proxy is the dependable setup (Run the downloads from a mirror, Proxies and certificate authorities, component by component).
data.the-distributor-log-shows-sha-256-mismat:
Symptom: runner-distributor: SHA-256 mismatch for circleci-runner_linux_amd64.tar.gz : got , wanted : refusing to install. The distributor installs nothing and retries later.
Cause. The tarball does not have the SHA-256 that the manifest, or your MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_SHA256 list, names. Usual causes: a list that lacks one architecture (a fleet with amd64 and arm64 nodes needs both), a mirror whose tarball and manifest do not match, or a proxy that changes the download.
Fix. Compare wanted with the SHA-256 of the file you expect, from the checksums.txt of the release or the manifest, and correct the list, mirror or proxy. Never copy the got value into the list without checking where the file came from.
data.the-runner-log-shows-401#The runner log:
Symptom: the log contains 401 (Unauthorized) and the runner never claims a job.
Cause. CircleCI rejected the token: it was deleted, mistyped, or belongs to another class. A drifted clock is not a 401: it fails the TLS handshake first (see the x509 entry).
Fix. Check that the secret -token holds the token of the class with the same name as the service. A swapped token does not fail loudly: the runner serves the class of its token, so jobs of the intended class stay queued. The token of a single-task class is in the proxy: look in runners_token-proxy (Windows: runners_token-proxy-windows) for upstream status 401. Then rotate the token.
data.the-runner-log-shows-403-and-the-proxy-l:
Symptom: the runner log has 403 (Forbidden) for the claim, and runners_token-proxy says claim from refused.
Cause. The proxy answers a claim only from an address that Swarm DNS lists now for tasks. of a class it serves, once for each container. The log line gives the reason.
Fix.
not a runner of any class: the class is not in the proxy (a new class needs its secret and, on Linux, its network under token-proxy: Define a class), the proxy is not on the class network, or the caller is not a runner.
this runner has already claimed a task: the proxy restarted while the runner was idle, moved to another node and lost its state, or latched the runner after a claim of unknown outcome (fail closed). The runner retries every 5 seconds until its idle timeout replaces it. On Linux, replace the idle runners now:
docker service update --force --update-parallelism 0 runners_ On Windows, do not: it kills busy jobs. Remove only the refused containers (Replace refused runners on Windows). See also A claim whose outcome is unknown and Restart the proxy.
too many claims (429), or 503 with Retry-After: the proxy limits each client IP and serves at most 512 requests at once. A runner stays far below that, so look for a client that polls in a loop (Monitor the token proxy).
data.the-runner-log-shows-x509-certificate-er:
Symptom: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid, or x509: certificate signed by unknown authority, and the runner never connects.
Cause. The node clock drifted, or an inspecting proxy re-signs the traffic with a CA that the container does not trust.
Fix. This must print yes. If not, fix NTP on the node.
timedatectl show -p NTPSynchronized --value For an inspecting proxy or your own CircleCI server CA, add the CA to your image for the runner and the jobs. The token proxy and the distributors read other stores: see Proxies and certificate authorities, component by component and Private certificate authorities.
data.the-runner-never-starts-cannot-access-pa:
Symptom: docker service ps --no-trunc runners_windows-default shows tasks failing with cannot access path ...\runner-bin\_data\current (or ...\git\current) or invalid mount config, and Swarm starts the next task after 10 seconds.
Cause. runner-distributor-windows has not flipped the links current and git\current of the volume on this node yet. This is normal on a new node (the first download of the runner and portable Git takes a few minutes). It lasts when the distributor cannot install.
Fix. Read its log:
docker service logs runners_runner-distributor-windows A SHA-256 mismatch, cannot download or not adopting it line names the cause. The service must have a task on the node (docker service ps runners_runner-distributor-windows), so the node needs the label machine-runner-swarm.windows-ltsc2022=true and the base image pulled. Behind a proxy, set HTTPS_PROXY on the distributor service (it reads only HTTPS_PROXY, no NO_PROXY). Without internet access, refer to Upgrade the runner on Windows.
data.the-runner-waits-for-the-distributor-and:
Symptom: the runner log shows circleci-runner-entrypoint: waiting for the runner-distributor of this node to install the runner. After the wait (120 seconds by default) the container exits with code 80 and /opt/machine-runner-swarm/current is 'missing': the runner-distributor of this node has not installed the runner, and the loop repeats every 10 seconds.
Cause. The runner-bin volume of the node has no runner yet: the runner-distributor task of the node is not running, cannot download the runner, or refuses it. A first deploy or a node that just joined is normal: the next container starts as soon as current exists.
Fix. Check that the distributor runs on that node, and read its log:
docker service ps --no-trunc runners_runner-distributor docker service logs --tail 50 runners_runner-distributor A node with no task is Down, drained, or not a Linux node. Otherwise see The distributor log shows cannot download and The distributor log shows SHA-256 mismatch. To wait longer, set MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_WAIT in the environment of the runner services.
data.the-token-proxy-service-does-not-start-t:
Symptom: docker service ps runners_token-proxy --no-trunc (Windows: runners_token-proxy-windows) shows No such image, manifest unknown, pull access denied or no matching manifest for , and runners get connection errors for token-proxy. The distributor and runner are unaffected.
Cause. The image is ccilabs/machine-runner-swarm-proxy, or what MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_PROXY_IMAGE names. Usual causes: the node cannot reach Docker Hub, the tag does not exist (a typo, or edge before the first publication of the main branch), a local image such as machine-runner-swarm-proxy:dev that exists on another node, or a platform the tag lacks (Windows on Arm).
Fix. Check the name and pull it on the node:
docker service inspect runners_token-proxy --format '{{.Spec.TaskTemplate.ContainerSpec.Image}}' docker pull Behind an allow list, add Docker Hub (Egress hosts), or mirror the image and set MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_PROXY_IMAGE (Upgrade the token proxy). A local build must be on the node that runs the proxy: build it there, or docker save | ssh docker load. Swarm retries by itself.
data.windows#Windows: Symptom Cause and fix Task rejected with 0xc0370101: The container operating system does not match the host operating system The image build is newer than the host. A Server 2022 host runs only ltsc2022 images, a Server 2025 host ltsc2025 and ltsc2022. Labels normally prevent this, so look for a node with a label it should not have. Use a tag the host can run, and set the machine-runner-swarm.windows-ltsc2022 and windows-ltsc2025 labels to match (Image tags and host builds) The container runs but the runner never claims a job and logs no clear error Without SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege the runner retries the task agent download forever. This happens when the container runs as a user other than ContainerAdministrator. Never set user: in a Windows service or change USER in a derived image Log says circleci-runner is in use: removing it at a later check Windows cannot remove files that a running container uses. Nothing to do: the distributor removes the version at a later check docker swarm init fails with could not find the system's IP address - specify one with --advertise-addr Pass the host IPv4 address: docker swarm init --advertise-addr (also on a host with several adapters, and Setup.ps1 -InitSwarm requires -AdvertiseAddr) Downloads fail with Unable to connect to the remote server or no such host for a few seconds after docker swarm init Pull the images first and run docker swarm init last. The distributor retries its downloads Overlay network creation fails on a host with one adapter An existing transparent network can block overlay networks. Move it to a second adapter or remove it (Microsoft documentation on Windows container networking) The first task on a host takes a long time The node pulls the Server Core image (about 2.2 GB compressed) when the first task lands. Run docker pull for the image on each node before you deploy Setup.ps1 reports CHECK windows-server FAIL The helper supports Windows Server 2022 (build 20348) and 2025 (build 26100). Server 2019 is untested and has no label in the stack files, so it needs your own image tag, label and constraint persist_to_workspace or attach_workspace reports a missing tar or gzip The Git mount is missing, or the service PATH lacks C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin (a service PATH replaces the image one). Keep both mounts and the full PATH from the shipped file C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin\tar.exe fails with Cannot stat when you run it by hand with a backslash path The task agent runs this tar.exe from the drive root with --force-local and forward-slash operands relative to the root (for C:\cci\w\ws it passes cci/w/ws). Use the same form in your test hcs::System::Start: context deadline exceeded An image build used New-Item -Force on an existing registry key, which deletes its values and subkeys. On HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\cexecsvc that removes the container exec service. Rebuild the image and set values with reg add or Set-ItemProperty

data: Changelog: Release notes are on GitHub Releases. Read every release between yours and the one you install before you upgrade. Migrate from Docker Compose: Move from the old docker-compose.yml setup to the Docker Swarm stack, and map each Compose setting to its Swarm equivalent.

The release notes are on GitHub Releases. Read the notes of every release between yours and the one that you install before you upgrade: the project follows Semantic Versioning and starts at 0.x, so a minor release can contain breaking changes, which the notes list first.
A CircleCI job writes the notes of each release from the Conventional Commits on main, with the rules in cliff.toml. Nobody edits this file by hand, and the release job never commits to main. Each release bundle contains a CHANGELOG.md with the notes of every release, and you can create the same text with git cliff. Refer to Releasing for how versions and notes are made, and to Contributing for the commit types and for how to mark a breaking change.

Warning Machine runner swarm no longer ships the Docker Compose setup. The files docker-compose.yml, base-image/, convenience-image/, and machine-image/ were removed in the Swarm rewrite, and the change is marked [BREAKING] in the changelog. Find the old files with git log -- docker-compose.yml.
The old setup restarted the same container after each job, so jobs did not get a clean environment. The Swarm stack creates a new container for every job (Why not plain Docker Compose?). This page covers Linux hosts, which the old setup supported. Your job configs, resource classes and tokens can stay.
data.behavior-to-expect#Behavior to expect: Runner updates. The runner is an exact pin by default: the newest version that CI tests, bumped by each release. Set 3.1, 3 or current to follow CircleCI’s manifest (Upgrade the runner on Linux). Sudo. The default classes keep passwordless sudo, as the old images did. The hardened class removes it (Concepts). Fixed replicas. The stack does not scale by itself, and a node that dies is not replaced (Capacity and concurrency). Startup time. A new container starts for every job, so a job waits about 10 seconds longer for the next claim, plus the task agent download. Add replicas for busy classes. Swarm on one host. Swarm mode is required even on a single host. The helper and the install page start it on the loopback address, so nothing is exposed. Working directory. The runner no longer removes the working directory on Linux, because it runs as another user than the jobs. A new container for every job leaves nothing behind, but a persistent class (the old machine service) keeps files between jobs, so start its jobs with a cleanup step (Working directory cleanup).
data.migrate#Migrate:
Name the classes. A Swarm service must have the name of its resource class. To keep your classes and tokens, name each service after the class it replaces, for example base. For new classes, create them.
Prepare the host. Docker Engine is already there. Start Swarm and install nothing else: the runner-distributor service installs the runner on every node (Start Swarm).
Create the secrets. Use the token of each class, the value of CIRCLECI_RUNNER_API_AUTH_TOKEN in your old .env file (Create the secrets).
Choose the images. The old convenience service maps to cimg/base or another cimg image, and base to a stock image with your tools. Move extra tools from your Dockerfiles into a derived image (Linux: bring your own image).
Edit the stack file. Rename or copy the services, set your old replica counts, and keep only what you need. The old machine service becomes linux/stack/persistent.yaml (Resource classes).
Deploy next to the old setup. Both can run at once, because the runner names differ. Check that the new runners show up in the inventory. If a new service keeps a class whose old runners are busy, the token proxy sees running tasks at its first start, cannot tell whose they are, and refuses the present runners until their idle timeout, or until you run the command below once the old runners are idle. New classes avoid this (Restart the proxy).
docker service update --force --update-parallelism 0 runners_ Stop the old setup. When the old runners are idle, run docker compose down in the old directory. A running job is stopped after the Compose grace period, so wait for a quiet period.
Clean up. Delete the old .env files, which hold tokens in clear text. If you created new classes, delete the old tokens and classes in CircleCI.
data.what-changed#What changed: Old setup Swarm stack Services base, convenience, and machine in docker-compose.yml One service for each resource class in linux/stack/runners.yaml. The continuous runner is linux/stack/persistent.yaml restart: unless-stopped, which restarts the same container restart_policy: condition: any, which creates a new container Token in a .env file as CIRCLECI_RUNNER_API_AUTH_TOKEN, visible in docker inspect Swarm secret -token, which holds a runner config file The same CIRCLECI_RUNNER_NAME for every replica {{.Node.Hostname}}--{{.Task.Slot}}, unique for each replica Dockerfiles that build the runner into an image A stock image, with the runner mounted from the volume runner-bin (Images) CIRCLECI_RUNNER_MODE and CIRCLECI_RUNNER_CLEANUP_WORK_DIR in the service environment The same variables, in the stack file. Cleanup is "false" on Linux

data:
This page lists what the stack protects, what it does not, and which controls you must apply on the CircleCI side. Read it before you give a class to a team.
Important Untrusted jobs on a self-hosted runner pose significant risks to your machines and your network. Never use self-hosted runners for public projects that build forked pull requests.
Status. Version 0.x, not independently reviewed or penetration-tested. The site follows main, so it can describe a control that your release does not have: use the copy of this page in your release bundle for that release. What is tested says how each claim is checked.
data.bitlocker-on-windows-hosts#BitLocker on:
Docker keeps a Swarm secret in clear text on the container root disk until the container stops. Encrypt the volume that holds the Docker root directory (C:\ProgramData\docker by default) with BitLocker, and confirm the protection status:
Get-BitLockerVolume The status of the volume must show that protection is on. BitLocker protects the token when someone steals the disk, or a snapshot or backup of it. It does not protect against a job, or an administrator who is logged in to the live host, because both read the decrypted file. Limit the local administrators of the host, use one token for each class and host, and rotate tokens. See the Microsoft documentation for BitLocker on Windows Server for the setup steps, including the recovery key.
data.circleci-server#CircleCI server: CircleCI documents machine runner 3 for server 4.4 and later, and says that an install on server sets the API URL of the runner (CIRCLECI_RUNNER_API_URL, or api.url in the config file). Machine runner swarm is tested against CircleCI cloud only. Here the runners call the token proxy, so the URL of your server goes to the -upstream argument of the token-proxy service (its command in the stack file), and the runners keep CIRCLECI_RUNNER_API_URL: http://token-proxy:8080. Whether the proxy and the runner download work against your server version is not known, and no job of this project has run against one. Config policies need the Scale plan on cloud or server 4.2 or later.
data.circleci-side-controls#CircleCI-side con:
The stack cannot decide which projects may use a class. Apply these controls in your organization.
One class and one token for each service. Give each token a nickname that names its host or purpose, so you can revoke it alone. Only organization admins create and delete resource classes. Delete the tokens of a class before the class.
Config policies. Restrict each class to named projects with the resource_class_by_project helper. Config policies need the Scale plan on cloud, or server version 4.2 or later. A class that is not in the mapping stays available to every project.
package org import data.circleci.config policy_name["runner_policies"] enable_hard["resource_class_check"] resource_class_check = config.resource_class_by_project({ "/linux-hardened": {""}, "/linux-docker-build": {"", ""} }) Enable evaluation and push the policy (Config policies for self-hosted runner):
circleci policy settings set --org --enabled circleci policy push ./config-policies --org Context restrictions. Project restrictions, security groups, and expression restrictions combine with logical AND. Restrict every context that jobs on a runner class use. For deploy contexts, add an expression such as pipeline.git.branch == "main" and not job.ssh.enabled.
No fork builds on public projects. CircleCI does not make self-hosted runners available to public projects that have Build forked pull requests enabled.
SSH rerun stays off unless a class needs it. The shipped classes leave CIRCLECI_RUNNER_SSH_ADVERTISE_ADDR unset and publish no ports. If you deploy the SSH add-on stack file, keep its class for named projects and restrict inbound port 54782 with the DOCKER-USER chain or a cloud security group (Rerun job with SSH).
Monitoring. Watch the runner inventory for names you do not know, and the logs for 401 and for exit code 80. In the log of the token proxy, a refused claim comes from a container that is not a runner of a class, or from a runner that tries to claim twice (Monitor the token proxy).
Runner classes are usable only by jobs of the organization that owns them.
data.cloud-nodes-block-the-metadata-address#C:
Nothing in this stack or in Docker stops a job from reaching the instance-metadata service that cloud providers serve at 169.254.169.254. On a cloud VM, it can hand out the credentials of the role attached to the node and, on some clouds, the user data of the instance. A job that reads them acts as the node. This is true of every self-hosted runner on a cloud VM.
These recipes are the usual ones, and CI does not test them. Check them on your own nodes with a job that runs curl -m 3 http://169.254.169.254/, which must fail.
Give the node role the fewest permissions that the node needs, often none. Do not leave the Swarm join token readable in the user data or startup script of an instance: a job that reaches the metadata service reads it, and with it joins a node to your Swarm.
Block the address for containers on Linux. Add a rule to the DOCKER-USER chain, which Docker evaluates before its own rules for container traffic:
sudo iptables -I DOCKER-USER -d 169.254.169.254 -j DROP Docker creates the chain when it starts, so add the rule after Docker is up, and again after a reboot. This systemd unit starts after docker.service and adds the rule only when it is missing:
[Unit] Description=Block the instance metadata address for containers After=docker.service Requires=docker.service [Service] Type=oneshot RemainAfterExit=yes ExecStart=/bin/sh -c 'iptables -C DOCKER-USER -d 169.254.169.254 -j DROP 2>/dev/null || iptables -I DOCKER-USER -d 169.254.169.254 -j DROP' [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target The rule does not cover a container on the host network (the docker-build class can use one) or the host itself. Check it with sudo iptables -S DOCKER-USER after a reboot and after a restart of Docker. If your Docker uses another firewall backend, use its equivalent.
On AWS, require IMDSv2 and a hop limit of 1. This disables IMDSv1 and stops the session-token response from reaching a container behind Docker’s bridge or NAT:
aws ec2 modify-instance-metadata-options --instance-id --http-tokens required --http-put-response-hop-limit 1 --http-endpoint enabled It does not cover containers on the host network. It also breaks every job that uses the node role through the metadata service: give such jobs their credentials another way, for example through a context or OIDC.
On other clouds, allow the metadata service from the host only, and attach a role with minimal permissions. On Windows nodes these settings apply too, but have not been tried with Windows containers.
data.compared-with-the-official-runner-instal:
The first three columns are our reading of the public CircleCI documentation as of 17 October 2026. They are not statements by CircleCI, the pages change, and the sources below are the reference. The last two columns come from the tests of this repository. Where the public documentation says nothing, the cell says so.
Machine runner 3 package Container runner Machine runner orchestrator Machine runner swarm, default class Machine runner swarm, hardened class Can a job read the class token? A job gains the privileges of the task agent, and the runner runs as the same user (circleci) Not stated. The agent holds the tokens in a Kubernetes secret No: a sidecar keeps the token out of the VM No, even with sudo: the token proxy holds it. A job that escapes onto the node of the proxy could read it No, for the same reason. The persistent class is the exception (The persistent class) Can jobs use sudo? Whatever you grant the circleci user Set by the job image and the pod securityContext No by default (grantSudo: false) Yes, passwordless, as in the Docker executor No: the step-down uses setpriv --no-new-privs Boundary between jobs None: each job runs on the machine where the runner is installed An ephemeral pod, on the shared node kernel A virtual machine for each job A new container for each job, on a shared kernel The same Sources: Self-hosted runner concepts, Self-hosted runner overview, Container runner reference, and the Machine runner orchestrator reference, including its sidecar and grantSudo.
A clean container is not a virtual machine. The orchestrator is the only column with a hardware-level boundary between jobs. If jobs must not share a kernel, use the orchestrator, or dedicate nodes to one trust group (Why Swarm and not container runner or another runner?). The token. The single-task classes here work like the orchestrator’s sidecar, except that a job that escapes onto the node of the proxy reaches the tokens. The persistent class and Windows are weaker: the token is a file in the container (Windows). The Windows persistent class is at parity with the official Windows runner, and the Windows classes have no hardened variant.
data.egress-hosts#Egress hosts:
Runners need outbound HTTPS only, and no inbound access. Allow these hosts by name, because their addresses change.
Host Port Used for runner.circleci.com 443 The runner API. With the token proxy, only the node of the proxy calls it for the single-task classes circleci-binary-releases.s3.amazonaws.com 443 The task agent, which every new container downloads, and the runner download (by runner-distributor, runner-distributor-windows, or each container of a microVM class) circleci-tasks-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com 443 Caches, workspaces, artifacts, and test results internal.circleci.com 443 Not on CircleCI’s list of hosts for self-hosted runners (the two hosts above, the cache host, and your VCS host). Allow it only if a job log shows that a step needs it Your VCS host, for example github.com 443, and 22 for SSH checkouts Checkout. For Bitbucket Cloud over SSH, CircleCI’s changelog says the agent uses ssh.bitbucket.org from 12 November 2026 Your image registries, for example Docker Hub and mcr.microsoft.com 443 Pulling the service images, on Linux also the alpine image of runner-distributor. The token proxy image comes from Docker Hub (registry-1.docker.io, auth.docker.io and its content delivery network), or from a mirror that you name with MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_PROXY_IMAGE github.com and release-assets.githubusercontent.com 443 On Windows, Git for Windows and 7-Zip, which runner-distributor-windows downloads (not in an air-gapped setup with a mirror). The first host redirects the downloads to the second If your VCS organization uses an IP allow list, add the egress addresses of your nodes.
